AI CLI Tools Community Digest 2026-11-21

Generated: 2026-11-21 02:06 UTC | Tools covered: 7

  • Claude Code
  • OpenAI Codex
  • Gemini CLI
  • GitHub Copilot CLI
  • OpenCode
  • Pi
  • Qwen Code

Cross-Tool Comparison

Cross-Tool Comparison Report: AI CLI Developer Tools Ecosystem

Date: 2026-11-21 Sources: Community digests for Claude Code, OpenAI Codex, Gemini CLI, GitHub Copilot CLI, OpenCode, Pi, and Qwen Code

1. Ecosystem Overview

The AI CLI tooling landscape on 2026-11-21 is characterized by rapid iteration on agentic runtimes coupled with a persistent drag from platform-specific regressions — particularly on Windows and macOS desktop. Vendors are converging on a common feature set (subagents, MCP, cross-session memory, remote control), but differentiation is increasingly expressed through execution reliability, permission/safety models, and enterprise readiness rather than raw model access. Release cadence is high across the board (four of seven tools shipped in the last 24h), yet the highest-engagement threads remain unresolved correctness bugs rather than new features. A notable structural signal: Qwen Code now spends a disproportionate share of maintainer bandwidth on CI gate stability (one issue at 506 comments), while Copilot CLI and OpenCode surface serious destructive-command and permission-enforcement incidents. Across all seven communities, the dominant trust battles are session continuity, quota/cost transparency, and safety guardrails that don't false-positive.

2. Activity Comparison

Tool Hot Issues (window) PR Activity (24h) Discussions Release Status
Claude Code 10 flagged (top: 31 comments, 👍38) 1 PR (security hardening, closed) N/A v2.1.330 (Enterprise Admin Console sign-in, easel mod)
OpenAI Codex 10 flagged (top: 75 comments) 11 PRs (sandbox, OAuth, MCP prewarm, protocol) Active — 4 Ideas, 3 Q&A, 4 Show-and-tell 4 alphas (rust-v0.173.0-alpha.1–.4)
Gemini CLI 10 flagged (top: 13 comments, 👍8) 10 PRs (sec/reliability, mostly closed) N/A v0.71.0-nightly.20261121
GitHub Copilot CLI 10 flagged (top: 8 comments on #5478) 0 PRs updated N/A 3 patches (v1.0.115-2/3/4)
OpenCode 10 flagged (top: 24 comments, 👍7) 10+ PRs (CI repair, sandbox, MCP events) N/A No release in window
Pi 10 flagged (3× P0 regressions) 10+ PRs (Windows, Bedrock, catalog perf) 1 Show-and-tell v1.6.0 (GPT-6.2 Astra/Sol, default Sol)
Qwen Code 10 flagged (top: 506 comments on CI gate) 10+ PRs (managed-agent, Web Shell, i18n) N/A v0.28.3 + preview + nightly (CI/test hardening)

Notes:

  • Discussions disabled/unused: Claude Code, Gemini CLI, Copilot CLI, OpenCode, and Qwen Code provide no Discussions data in this window and are marked N/A rather than inactive.
  • Copilot CLI is a special case — Issues are enabled but PRs are not visible upstream (PR count = 0), reflecting a closed-development model with community feedback via issues only.
  • Claude Code shows only one PR in the window, indicating either a strict PR-gating policy or external contributions routed elsewhere; not a sign of low internal velocity given the v2.1.330 ship.

3. Shared Feature Directions

The following requirements recur across ≥3 communities, indicating ecosystem-level demand rather than vendor-specific quirks:

Direction Tools Requesting Specific Need
Cross-session memory / continuity Claude Code (#102045, #85657), Codex (#12567 Memories — highest-engagement thread), Pi (#11055 hook control), Qwen Code (#17910 transcript retention) Durable, citable, project-scoped memory that survives session boundaries; external "canonical state" layers proposed by both Codex and Claude Code users.
Subagent visibility & control OpenCode (#64073 — 24 comments), Gemini CLI (#22323, #21763, #22598), Claude Code (#100347 sub-agent params) Foreground/background toggles, trajectory exposure via share commands, accurate termination-status reporting (no silent MAX_TURNS masking).
MCP robustness & protocol completeness Copilot CLI (#4203 OAuth refresh, #5050 case-insensitivity, #5542 status probe), Codex (#62631 status/list, #62871 metadata), OpenCode (#64117 tools/list_changed), Gemini CLI (#24246 >128 tools) Token lifecycle correctness, dynamic tool registration, catalog status reporting, and scaling beyond ~128-tool surfaces.
Permission-model simplification Copilot CLI (#5539, #5066, #5541), OpenCode (#65290 external_directory bypass), Gemini CLI (#22672 destructive commands, #18397 workspace policy), Codex (#62882 managed domain rules) Persistent user-level rules over per-repo duplication; confirmation gates for destructive ops; rules that are actually enforced (not silently bypassed).
Cost / quota / cache transparency Copilot CLI (#5220 1h Claude cache, +17👍), Codex (#59398 quota), Pi (#12308 cost accounting), Qwen Code (#17902 token ledger) Accurate token accounting, configurable prompt-cache TTLs, non-opaque rate-limit depletion, aligned exit codes for CI pipelines.
Cross-platform / remote parity Claude Code (#110673 Desktop Code Mode, #95364 Remote Control), Codex (#62877, #62472, #61904 remote/history), Copilot CLI (#5468 GitHub Mobile), OpenCode (#65214 Windows shell) Consistent behavior across CLI, Desktop, web, and mobile; history sync across authorized devices; remote sessions that survive updates.
Localization / IME / non-Latin input Gemini CLI (#30178 Korean IME), OpenCode (#55676 Cyrillic keybinds), Qwen Code (#17437 Arabic + RTL), Pi (#11383 ANSI paste) Correct commit behavior on IME-contiguous input, layout-agnostic keybind matching, RTL layout support.

Emerging (2 communities, worth watching): Sandbox architecture as a first-class primitive (OpenCode #65168 experimental foundation; Codex #62882/#62865 managed domain rules + Windows sandbox owner restoration). This suggests a shift from per-command approval toward declarative capability sandboxes.

4. Differentiation Analysis

Claude Code — Enterprise-first, governance-oriented. The v2.1.330 Enterprise Admin Console sign-in and org-routed cloud/gateway support signal a deliberate pivot toward managed deployment. Its community, however, is dominated by TUI regressions (scrollback duplication 👍38, 7 months open) and session-lifecycle transparency issues. Target user: enterprise teams needing org policy and audit trails. Weakness: TUI durability and auth-support dead ends (#79808 — a paying user locked out with no escalation).

OpenAI Codex — Aggressive alpha velocity, desktop-heavy. Four alphas in 24h and 11 PRs indicate fast iteration on the Rust agent core, sandboxing, and app-server protocol. But its pain profile is the most acute: two macOS launch-blocking crashes (#62650 wallpaper tint; #62856 profile-specific) plus two Windows hang classes (#62731 MSIX; #60484 WSL PATH probe on the main thread). Target user: power users on desktop with multi-device remote workflows. Weakness: release-quality gating — users report downgrading.

Gemini CLI — Subagent subsystem as the center of gravity. Issues cluster heavily around agent/subagent correctness (hangs, silent success masking, browser-agent Wayland failures). BigSmoKe07's security PR burst (dangerous-rm flag-position bypass, pasted-@ secret attachment) shows a focused hardening push on tool-invocation safety. Target user: developers leveraging Gemini's native bash affinity. Weakness: subagent reliability and configuration being ignored (#22267 Browser Agent bypassing settings.json).

GitHub Copilot CLI — MCP and Windows enterprisization. A three-patch day focused on Windows sandboxing and plugin init races, while the backlog is dominated by MCP OAuth lifecycle and enterprise EDR interference (#5478 Cortex XDR killing spawned git). The #5541 rsync --delete WSL incident is the most severe safety report across all seven tools. Target user: GitHub-ecosystem enterprise devs, IDE-adjacent workflows. Weakness: destructive-command guardrails and MCP auth brittleness in unattended/CI flows.

OpenCode (anomalyco) — Open-source velocity with Windows broken-window risk. No release in the window but heavy PR flow: CI repair, MCP Events beta (SEP-3415), experimental agent sandbox, session full-text search. The pain cluster is explicit v2.3.2 regressions on Windows (empty shell output, %USERPROFILE% desktop opening, double-quote escaping). Target user: OSS developers and tinkerers who value SDK/API control. Weakness: release-cycle discipline (2.3.2 cited across many issues).

Pi (earendil-works) — Provider-agnostic reasoning fidelity. v1.6.0's GPT-6.2 Sol-default rollout landed with two P0 regressions within 24h (#12361 thinking-effort downgrade to "medium"; #12367 prefix_mismatch reasoning drops), plus Anthropic Team/Enterprise OAuth scope rejection (#12318). Its distinctive concern is cross-provider consistency — --thinking must map to each provider's native controls. Target user: multi-provider developers. Weakness: post-release regression testing on provider compatibility paths.

Qwen Code — Managed-agent runtime maturity + CI gate crisis. Three builds sharing one change set (managed-agent E2E + verify-pr hardening) reveal the real investment: a server-side managed agent with Broker/Control Plane, runtime-owned background observation, and Web Shell migration. Meanwhile #14724 at 506 comments is a chronic CI gate failure re-firing per commit — the most extreme maintainer-bandwidth sink in the set. Target user: large-repo teams and China-ecosystem channel integrations (DingTalk, Teams, QQ). Weakness: CI gate instability blocking required-check adoption.

5. Community Momentum & Maturity

Momentum ranking (iteration velocity × engagement):

Tier Tools Evidence
Very high velocity OpenAI Codex, Qwen Code Codex: 4 alphas + 11 PRs in 24h. Qwen: 3 builds + 10+ stacked managed-agent PRs. Qwen's 506-comment CI thread also reflects intense (if costly) activity.
High velocity Pi, OpenCode, Gemini CLI Pi: v1.6.0 + follow-up PR cascade. OpenCode: 10+ PRs and experimental sandbox without a release. Gemini CLI: nightly + BigSmoKe07 security burst.
Steady / patch-focused Claude Code, Copilot CLI Claude Code: one meaningful release + one PR (gatekeeping model). Copilot: 3 patches, no PRs visible upstream.

Community health signals:

  • Healthiest feedback loops: Codex (Discussions actively used for memory design), Pi (community OAuth shim #12364 offered as workaround), Copilot CLI (#2109 ACP request shipped in v1.0.115-4 — a clear community win).
  • Maturity signals: Claude Code and Copilot CLI show enterprise-grade governance (admin console, sandbox capabilities toggles), but at the cost of slower community responsiveness.
  • At-risk signals: Qwen Code's 506-comment CI issue and repeated "no test identified" failures indicate process debt consuming contributor cycles. OpenCode's concentrated 2.3.2 regressions suggest release QA gaps.

Maturity vs. velocity trade-off: The enterprise-leaning tools (Claude Code, Copilot CLI) are the most stable but least responsive; the high-velocity tools (Codex, Pi, Qwen) deliver features fastest but absorb regression pain in public.

6. Trend Signals

For technical decision-makers:

  1. Desktop is the new reliability frontier. Launch-blocking desktop regressions at Codex (macOS wallpaper tint, Windows MSIX hang), Claude Code (stealth-update killing remote sessions), and OpenCode (Windows shell/path failures) suggest vendor QA still prioritizes CLI over the GUI surface. Teams standardizing on desktop clients should pin versions and maintain rollback paths.

  2. Safety guardrails are bifurcating into two problems — false negatives (Copilot CLI #5541 rsync --delete data loss; Copilot #5066 over-prompting) and false positives (Claude Code's six closed [Bug][cyber] reports from a legitimate embedded-firmware developer; Gemini CLI's pasted-@ secret attachment capability). Expect vendors to converge on dry-run defaults + confirmation gates + declarative sandboxes rather than binary allow/deny.

  3. Cross-session memory is the next competitive battleground. Codex's #12567 survey, Claude Code's continuity complaints, and Pi/Qwen transcript work all point the same direction. The differentiator will be citable (attributable) memory with project-scoping — a security-relevant design choice, not just a convenience feature.

  4. Windows is systematically under-served. Every tool with a Windows footprint reports a dedicated pain cluster: EDR interference (Copilot), Cygwin argument truncation at 8,186 chars (Pi), WSL PATH probe hangs (Codex), argv 32,767-char limit (Qwen), empty shell output (OpenCode), path expansion bugs (Gemini CLI). For Windows-majority enterprises, this is the single most actionable diligence item.

  5. Permission enforcement is becoming a trust/security issue, not UX. OpenCode's external_directory bypass (#65290, severity:high) and cross-machine approval leakage (#65295) plus Copilot's destructive-command incident show that permission systems are being bypassed in practice. Buyers evaluating agentic CLIs should audit whether configured rules are actually enforced, not just declared.

  6. MCP has crossed from "supported" to "expected to be robust." OAuth token lifecycle, dynamic tool registration, catalog status, and >128-tool scaling are now baseline requirements across Copilot CLI, Codex, OpenCode, and Gemini CLI. MCP reliability will be a differentiating selection criterion for teams running many servers.

  7. CI/MCP-in-CI is a growing blind spot. Copilot CLI's stricter CI exit codes on MCP startup failure (#3064), Pi's JSON-mode exit-code alignment (#12356), and Qwen's CI gate crisis all indicate that agentic CLIs are increasingly invoked from pipelines — where silent failures and nonzero-exit semantics matter more than interactive ergonomics.

Compiled 2026-11-21 from community digests for the seven referenced repositories. Comment/upvote counts reflect the snapshot provided and are directional, not exhaustive.

Per-Tool Reports

Claude Code — anthropics/claude-code

Claude Code Skills Highlights

Source: anthropics/skills

Claude Code Skills — Community Highlights Report

Data snapshot: 2026-11-21 · Source: github.com/anthropics/skills

1. Top Skills Ranking (Most-Discussed PRs)

Note: The PR dataset shows Comments: undefined for all top-20 entries, so ranking below is based on relative community attention inferred from update frequency, issue linkage, and cross-referencing with high-comment Issues.

# Skill / PR Functionality Discussion Highlight Status
1 mcp-builder fix (#1742) Fixes streamable_http_client import rename & custom header config for MCP ≥2.0 Breaks real MCP connections; tracked via Issue #1668. Bumped repeatedly (Sep→Oct). OPEN
2 skill-creator eval isolation (#1298) Fixes false trigger-eval misses; Windows subprocess + runtime failure handling Directly tied to the loudest eval bug (Issues #556, #1352). Long-lived since June. OPEN
3 notion-spec-to-implementation + quantitative-resume-auditor (#1245) Turns product specs into Notion tasks Claude can execute; plus resume auditing Two-for-one submission; active through Oct despite June creation. OPEN
4 webapp-testing: drop shell=True (#1980) Removes CWE-78 command-injection risk in with_server.py Security-hardening angle resonates with Issue #492 trust concerns. OPEN
5 docx: LibreOffice timeout → error (#1792) accept_changes.py now errors on timeout and verifies revision marks removed Silent-success bug fix; verified correctness matters for doc pipelines. OPEN
6 pyxel retro game skill (#525) Guides retro Python game dev: headless input runs, frame inspection, state checks Oldest still-active PR (Mar→Nov); niche but persistent. OPEN
7 xlsx: external link resolution (#2019) Fixes false negatives for worksheet-scoped defined names in recalc.py Fixes #2013; Oct–Nov activity shows ongoing spreadsheet pain. OPEN
8 document-typography (#514) Prevents orphan/widow text and numbering misalignment in generated docs Universal output-quality gap every user hits. OPEN

2. Community Demand Trends (from Issues)

Distilling the highest-comment Issues reveals five clear demand axes:

  1. Trust & namespace security — Issue #492 (46 comments, top of list) calls out community skills masquerading under the anthropic/ namespace, enabling privilege escalation. This is the single loudest concern.
  2. Skill sharing & org distribution — Issue #228 (17 comments, 👍8) wants org-wide skill libraries instead of manual .skill file passing via Slack.
  3. Trustworthy evaluation tooling — Issues #556 (0% trigger rate) and #1352 (parallel-worker cross-matching) expose that the skill-eval harness itself is unreliable — a meta-quality crisis.
  4. Context-budget governance — Issue #1487 reports claude-api eagerly injecting ~156k tokens in one call. Demand for lazy/on-demand skill loading.
  5. Reasoning & output quality gates — Issue #1385 proposes a pre-task calibration → adversarial review → delivery verification pipeline; #1143 (👍18, highest) shows platform-level frustration spilling into skills requests.

Emerging proposed directions: compact symbolic memory (#1329), agent-governance safety patterns (#412, closed), and description-quality linting (#2064).

3. High-Potential Pending Skills (Active, Unmerged)

These are the strongest candidates to land soon based on recency + breadth:

  • mcp-builder fix (#1742) — High impact, blocks real MCP users. Likely near-merge.
  • skill-creator direct execution (#1681) — Active to Nov 19; fixes ModuleNotFoundError on standalone runs. Complementary to #1298/#1997.
  • skill-creator YAML frontmatter parsing (#1997) — Correctness fix for eval metadata; clean scope.
  • webapp-testing element discovery (#1976) — Small, targeted fix (textarea/select reporting).
  • algorithmic-art wraparound (#1977) — Clean modulo fix, resolves #1897.
  • md2video-audio skill (#1703) — Zero-cost Markdown→MP4 with voiceover; novel content-generation addition.
  • scnet-hpc skill (#1615) — Slurm/SSH cluster operations for scientific computing; fills a real vertical gap.
  • notion-spec-to-implementation (#1245) — Product-spec→task automation; high workflow value if reviewers engage.

4. Skills Ecosystem Insight

The community's most concentrated demand is not for more Skills, but for a trustworthy Skill substrate — verified triggers, secure namespacing, honest error reporting, and context-efficient loading — before breadth can safely scale.

The top PRs and Issues converge on the same theme: fixes to existing tooling (skill-creator, mcp-builder, docx/xlsx scripts) vastly outnumber genuinely new Skill proposals, and the loudest open Issue (#492) is a trust-boundary vulnerability rather than a missing feature.

Claude Code Community Digest — 2026-11-21

1. Today's Highlights

Release v2.1.330 ships Enterprise Admin Console sign-in, letting claude auth login apply organization settings and route through the org's cloud provider or gateway — a notable step for enterprise adoption. Meanwhile, the issue tracker shows a cluster of long-running regressions (scrollback duplication, paste-handling bugs, session-resume quirks) that continue to accumulate comments months after filing. A new PR (#111198) closes a security-relevant gap by preventing @claude mentions on fork PRs from triggering runs.

2. Releases

v2.1.330 (release notes)

  • Added sign-in to organizations managed in Anthropic's Enterprise Admin Console: after claude auth login, Claude Code applies the organization's settings and uses its cloud provider or gateway.
  • Added "easel," a built-in mod that draws charts when asked and under MCP metrics results.

3. Hot Issues

  1. #79808 — Auth lockout with no escalation path (31 comments, 👍7, OPEN). A user's verification emails are suppressed and the support bot offers no human escalation — a severe blocker for a paying user, and the top-commented issue today.
  2. #51828 — Scrollback duplication on terminal resize (31 comments, 👍38, OPEN, regression). The highest-upvoted item in today's set, still persisting from 2.1.116 in VS Code's integrated terminal on macOS. Strong signal that this TUI regression is widely felt.
  3. #89690 — opusplan row silently dropped from model picker (23 comments, OPEN). A logic bug where the picker considers opusplan "already covered" by a built-in lineup that contains no Opus Plan Mode row — model selection correctness issue.
  4. #95364 — Desktop "stealth update" kills Remote Control sessions (22 comments, 👍24, OPEN). Auto-update quits and relaunches the app while the user is away, dropping every remote session — a workflow-breaking reliability issue for remote-control users.
  5. #85654 — Slash commands inside collapsed pastes never dispatch (8 comments, OPEN, reproduced). Pasted /command text is submitted as a plain message instead of executing — subtle but frustrating TUI correctness bug.
  6. #92434 — Auto-compact uses stale token counts (7 comments, OPEN). Re-injected instruction files can overflow the context window because compaction decisions lag a turn behind — a core context-management concern.
  7. #102045 — No project-decision memory across sessions (6 comments, OPEN). Claude Code forgets prior decisions even with the same session link — a recurring memory/continuity complaint on the web platform.
  8. #79223 — CLAUDE_SECURESTORAGE_CONFIG_DIR undocumented (4 comments, 👍3, OPEN). Ecosystem tooling widely relies on this credential-store override, but it's absent from env-var docs — a low-cost docs fix with outsized impact.
  9. #100004 — Resume after usage-limit retry produces synthetic "No response requested." (3 comments, OPEN). Resuming an interrupted session answers the pending message with a placeholder — confusing and potentially lossy behavior.
  10. #110673 — Code Mode in Desktop's Code tab (2 comments, 👍4, OPEN, enhancement). Experimental Code Mode only works in the interactive CLI; users want parity in the Desktop app — a clear platform-consistency request.

Also notable: a cluster of six [Bug][cyber] false-positive reports from user sworrl (#94166, #94164, #94163, #94162, #94161, #94167) were all closed today — safety filters blocking authorized embedded-firmware debugging, triaged as duplicates.

4. Key PR Progress

Only one PR was updated in the last 24 hours:

  1. #111198 — Don't run @claude mentions on pull requests from forks (CLOSED, by mhegazy). Prevents fork-originated PRs from triggering @claude runs — an important supply-chain/security hardening for anyone running the GitHub integration on public repos.

Note: the data source shows only this single PR updated in the window, so a larger "top 10" list cannot be provided without fabricating entries.

5. Hot Discussions

No Discussions data was provided in the source dataset — this section is omitted.

6. Feature Request Trends

Distilled from the issue set:

  • Cross-platform parity — Code Mode in Desktop's Code tab (#110673); desktop surfacing of on-disk transcripts for cross-machine continuity (#81835).
  • Session/memory continuity — retaining project decisions across sessions (#102045); resumable background sessions with correct semantics (#85657).
  • Composability of commands/skills — opt-in frontmatter letting custom slash commands expand into built-in command invocations (#91146).
  • Documentation completeness — credential-store path override (#79223); sub-agent effort and per-invocation model parameters (#100347).
  • Remote-control reliability — keeping Remote Control sessions alive across updates (#95364) and preventing auto-disable while away (#109419).

7. Developer Pain Points

  • Auth and support dead ends. Verification-email suppression with no escalation path (#79808) is the sharpest example of users being fully locked out with no recourse.
  • TUI regressions that linger. Scrollback duplication on resize (#51828, 7 months open, 👍38), paste-collapsed slash commands (#85654), and hidden assistant text during AskUserQuestion (#108098) erode trust in the terminal experience.
  • Session lifecycle surprises. Stale-token auto-compaction (#92434), synthetic "No response requested." on resume (#100004), and un-resumable sessionKind:bg entries (#85657) make resumption unpredictable.
  • Update/relaunch behavior breaks long-running work. Desktop stealth updates dropping Remote Control sessions (#95364) and Remote Control self-disabling on Windows (#109419) both punish users who step away.
  • Safety-filter false positives on legitimate work. The six closed [Bug][cyber] reports from one embedded-firmware developer show that overly broad safeguards can halt authorized engineering sessions.
  • Multi-account isolation gaps. Shared skill-sync buckets churning ~/.claude/skills/.trash across accounts (#98526) highlight friction for developers juggling multiple identities.

Digest generated from github.com/anthropics/claude-code activity for 2026-11-21. Comment/upvote counts reflect the snapshot provided.

OpenAI Codex — openai/codex

OpenAI Codex Community Digest — 2026-11-21

1. Today's Highlights

A new rust-v0.173.0-alpha.4 release continues the rapid alpha cadence for the 0.173 line. The community's attention is dominated by launch-blocking desktop app regressions on macOS and Windows (wallpaper tint crash, MSIX update hangs), plus a cluster of Codex Remote connectivity failures across iOS/macOS/Windows. A large batch of closed PRs from the copyberry[bot] pipeline shows internal work on sandboxing, OAuth, MCP prewarming, and app-server protocol refinements.

2. Releases

Four alpha builds shipped in the last 24 hours:

  • rust-v0.173.0-alpha.4
  • rust-v0.173.0-alpha.3
  • rust-v0.173.0-alpha.2
  • rust-v0.173.0-alpha.1

Release notes are terse (no changelog detail), but the rapid alpha iteration suggests active CLI/agent refactoring on the Rust side.

3. Hot Issues

  1. #57101 — Windows Computer Use leaves the capture border and access open after a turn completes. 75 comments, 👍13. Longest-running active thread; possible resource/permission leak in the unified CUA plugin.
  2. #62650 — macOS Codex App 26.1117.31558 crashes on launch in a wallpaper tint fallback. 👍16. Launch-blocking; affects default Apple wallpapers.
  3. #62856 — Separate macOS crash (NSUnknownKeyException) that reproduces only on one user profile. Strong signal of corrupted per-user state.
  4. #62472 [CLOSED] — Codex Remote WebSocket opens but initialize times out after 30s on macOS and Windows. Community-wide since Nov 17–18.
  5. #62877 — Codex Remote Control spinning/unavailable from iOS and macOS; matches the same Nov 20 window.
  6. #60484 — Windows Desktop hangs on startup due to a spawnSync bash -ilc WSL PATH probe with no timeout on the main thread. Clean, actionable root cause.
  7. #62731 — Windows app hangs (MoAppHang) on every launch after the MSIX update, reproducible with a fresh CODEX_HOME.
  8. #29809 — SSH reconnect leaks stale remote app-server processes across hosts, eventually hitting fork/exec failures. Long-running reliability issue.
  9. #59398 — Plus five-hour quota hits 98% in ~5 minutes with Astra medium and mostly cached long context. Quota accounting concern.
  10. #61548 — Windows Work mode: GPT-6.1 Sol stops at Max even with Ultra enabled. Model-tier selection bug on Windows.

Also notable: #62631 (MCP catalog rejects mcpServerStatus/list 156× in logs) and #61904 (iOS remote history empty while Windows shows the same host sessions).

4. Key PR Progress

  1. #62882 — Compose managed domain rules across [permissions.network], [network_proxy], and [experimental_network]. Fixes silent rule loss in managed configs.
  2. #62867 — Enable configuration server OAuth during app-server startup (--print-startup-config flow).
  3. #62859 — Protocol definition for startup OAuth, adding {"kind":"configServer"} as a target.
  4. #62865 — Defer Windows sandbox owner restoration until sign-in; hardens against missing sessions/tokens at boot.
  5. #62876 — Prewarm MCP servers during cloud catalog refresh to avoid first-turn latency.
  6. #62871 — Preserve per-image imageMetadata on app-server image generation items.
  7. #62863 — Send x-codex-exclude: tools to make Responses API omit the echoed tool catalog (wire-size reduction).
  8. #62857 — Defer Default-mode instructions until a thread actually uses Plan mode; reduces prompt noise.
  9. #62849 — Cut allocations in tool schema budget checks and Responses Lite catalog building.
  10. #62858 — Keep Cloud threads fresh in the Agents overview via Cloud stream notifications.
  11. #62852 — Cap guardian resampling to a single retry to prevent turn-stalling loops.

5. Hot Discussions

Ideas

  • #12567 — Memories in Codex (42 comments, 👍14). The team is surveying how cross-thread memory should be surfaced and cited. Highest-engagement thread today.
  • #33353 — Canonical project-state layer for ChatGPT Projects.
  • #44795 — Live integrations, secure sign-in, low-latency computer use.
  • #62661 — Open Temporary Chat in a separate window.

Q&A

  • #2503 — How to scroll terminal conversation history (👍38, still unanswered by docs — a recurring docs gap).
  • #37960 — Coordinating local + remote agents across model vendors.
  • #57029 — Multi-account Gmail plugin access.

Show and tell

  • #61475 — Ragmir: cited project context for Codex over code/PDF/Office.
  • #62545 — Open Agent API: call local Codex through an existing OpenAI SDK.
  • #62426 — TernaryCode: Rust-based multi-agent session monitor.
  • #1303 — Bell-sound notifications for Codex CLI (👍8).

6. Feature Request Trends

  • Cross-session memory / continuity — the Memories thread (#12567) plus multiple "boot protocol + external canonical state" proposals (#51228, #33353) show sustained demand for durable, citable memory.
  • Remote/mobile parity — across #61904, #62877, #62472, #60807: history sync, ghost chats, and reliable device handoff.
  • Quota transparency — #59398, #62880, #59428 all flag surprising or fast rate-limit depletion.
  • First-class integrations — #44795 and #40230 request a permission-scoped Codex↔ChatGPT bridge and a general integration layer.
  • Multi-agent orchestration — #37960 and related work on concurrency guidance and role-tagged instructions.
  • Better MCP tooling — prewarming, catalog status reporting (#62631), and per-image metadata (#62871).

7. Developer Pain Points

  • Desktop launch regressions are the top acute pain. macOS wallpaper-tint crash (#62650, 👍16), multi-user-only macOS crash (#62856), and two Windows hang classes (#62731, #60484) are all launch blockers introduced in recent updates; users report having to downgrade or change system settings.
  • Codex Remote reliability degraded around Nov 17–20: WebSocket opens, initialize times out (#62472), Remote Control spins (#62877). Users with multiple authorized devices see inconsistent history.
  • Windows/sandbox fragility — elevated sandbox reprovisioning on every local command (#62847), WSL integration blocking startup (#61546), and startup-path hangs caused by synchronous probes.

  1. #30174 — Stop body timeouts from killing and replaying long model turns (CLOSED) Fixes a 5-minute undici body timeout that aborted long single-turn generations (e.g., large write_file args at high thinking) and replayed them up to 3×.

  2. #30169 — Keep pasted @ text and fuzzy matches from attaching secrets (CLOSED, P1 security) Closes a real path where a pasted shell transcript could silently attach an SSH private key to a model request. ui.escapePastedAtSymbols now defaults to true.

  3. #30171 — Flag recursive and forced rm regardless of flag position (CLOSED, P1) Previously rm -r -f, rm -Rf, rm -vrf, rm --recursive --force x, and rm x -rf all evaded the dangerous-command policy engine. Important hardening.

No GitHub Discussions data was provided for this window — section omitted.

Distilled from the Issues set, the most-requested directions are:

  • Agent self-awareness & configurability — Accurate CLI flags/hotkeys self-description (#21432), honoring settings.json in all agents (#22267), and more proactive use of skills/subagents (#21968).
  • Context frugality & precision — AST-aware reads/search/mapping (#22745, #22746) and "Tactful Extraction" surgical read hierarchies (#19561) to control a ~36.6k-token baseline.
  • Persistent task tracking — Replacing in-context WriteToDo with file-based CRUD task tracking (#18836).
  • Subagent observability — Exposing subagent trajectories via /chat share (#22598) and richer subagent context in bug reports (#21763).

  • Subagent reliability and transparency. Hangs (#21409), silent MAX_TURNS masking (#22323), Wayland browser failures (#21983), and hidden subagent context (#21763) recur across the tracker. This is the single largest source of friction.
  • Configuration not being honored. settings.json overrides ignored by Browser Agent (#22267) and tool-count limits causing 400s (#24246) erode trust in the config surface.
  • Enterprise/paid-tier breakage. QUOTA_EXHAUSTED despite ample remaining quota (#29425) blocks Workspace Standard users despite active subscriptions.
  • Session and workspace hygiene. Models creating temp scripts in random directories (#23571), destructive git commands (#22672), and duplicate tool results in history (#30172) make clean commits and reproducible sessions harder than they should be.
  • Installation/auto-update misclassification. Project-local installs launched outside the project root trigger unintended global npm install -g (#30393, #30267, #30272) — an active cluster of fixes under review.

A busy release day: three patch releases (v1.0.115-2/3/4) landed hardening Windows sandboxing, macOS Mach service lookups, and fixing a plugin initialization race that could block or corrupt session resumption. The issue tracker is dominated by MCP reliability concerns — OAuth token lifecycle, Task augmentation, and server probe failures — alongside a serious new report (#5541) of an agent running a destructive rsync --delete command in WSL. Community attention is also converging on long-standing requests: 1-hour Claude prompt cache TTL (#5220, +17 👍) and ACP structured clarification questions, which just shipped in v1.0.115-4.

2. Releases

v1.0.115-4

  • Added: Structured clarification questions in ACP editors that support forms.
  • Fixed:
    • Plugin initialization race that blocked new sessions or prevented existing sessions from resuming.
    • Windows: child process cleanup for Git commands, hooks, and language server checks.

v1.0.115-3

v1.0.115-2

Note: v1.0.115-4 closes the long-standing ACP request in Issue #2109 — see Hot Issues below.

3. Hot Issues

  1. #5478 — Cortex XDR kills the shell when Copilot CLI spawns git (OPEN, 8 comments) On Windows, Cortex XDR flags parent_process_spoofing and terminates cmd/powershell when Copilot CLI invokes git. A hard blocker for enterprise users with EDR tooling — the highest-comment issue in the window.

  2. #5066 — Assisted permissions regression (CLOSED, 5 comments) Users report assisted-permissions mode demanding approval for trivially safe commands (e.g., a PowerShell directory listing). Now closed, but emblematic of the permission-UX friction discussed in #5539.

  3. #4203 — Remote MCP OAuth: expired access token forces interactive re-auth (OPEN, 5 comments, +5 👍) The CLI ignores a cached refresh token and forces a fresh OAuth login when the access token expires — dropping all server tools. Directly undermines the value of OAuth-protected MCP servers in unattended flows.

  4. #4805 — Stale inuse.<pid>.lock makes sessions unrevivable (OPEN, 4 comments) After a host crash, session lock files are never reclaimed, permanently bricking otherwise intact sessions. A data-loss-adjacent reliability bug that erodes trust in session persistence.

  5. #2109 — ACP: support an ask_user/ask_question extension method (CLOSED, 4 comments, +9 👍) The most-upvoted issue in this window, requesting structured clarification questions for custom ACP clients. Notably, v1.0.115-4 ships exactly this capability — a strong community win.

  6. #5220 — Option for 1-hour prompt cache TTL for Claude models (OPEN, 4 comments, +17 👍) The highest-👍 open issue: Anthropic's default 5-minute cache TTL routinely expires between interactive prompts, causing full-conversation re-billing. A concrete cost and latency pain point.

  7. #5090 — Boot experience + input line experience (OPEN, 3 comments) Users must wait for MCP/plugin loading before typing; the request is for async startup. Critical for large repos with many MCP servers.

  8. #5468 — Remote control fails on GitHub Mobile and github.com (OPEN, updated 2026-11-21, 2 comments) Relay connect fails with "sealed value must bind this connection's challenge." Sessions sync and read fine but cannot be controlled — a cross-surface regression affecting the mobile workflow.

  9. #5440 — Agent Plugins 1.0: .instructions.md and applyTo frontmatter silently ignored (OPEN) Plugin packaging loads skills/MCP/agents/hooks, but com.github.copilot/rules/ instruction files are dropped without warning. Silent failure is especially damaging to plugin authors.

  10. #5541 — Agent ran rsync -a --delete <dir>/ / in WSL, wiping a user drive (OPEN, triage) A quoting failure across the PowerShell→WSL boundary produced a catastrophic command. Zero-upvote so far, but the most severe safety incident reported — merits immediate guardrail discussion (e.g., destructive-command confirmation).

4. Key PR Progress

No pull requests were updated in the last 24 hours (total: 0 items), so there is no PR activity to report for this window.

5. Hot Discussions

No Discussions data was provided in the source feed, so this section is omitted.

6. Feature Request Trends

  • MCP robustness & protocol completeness: Silent refresh_token grant (#4203), Tasks augmentation for task-required tools (#5540), case-insensitive /mcp <server> matching (#5050), OAuth status probe fixes (#5542), and stricter CI exit codes on MCP startup failure (#3064).
  • Permission model simplification: One persistent, user-level read-access rule across sessions and repos instead of per-repo duplication or complex rules (#5539); fewer spurious approvals in assisted mode (#5066).
  • Session lifecycle & observability: Lock reclamation (#4805), AI-credit usage columns in session lists (#5537), and deterministic model/context-window switching (#5535).
  • Editor & terminal ergonomics: Multiline selection for comments in /diff (#5534), stable scroll position during streaming output (#5533), and ACP structured questions (#2109, now shipped).
  • Extension & workflow breadth: Browser-extension approval flow for non-Chromium/Edge browsers like Vivaldi (#5538).
  • Cost/latency controls: 1-hour Claude prompt cache TTL (#5220).

7. Developer Pain Points

  1. Destructive-command safety: The WSL rsync --delete incident (#5541) shows that quoting/escaping failures across shells can escalate into data loss. Users need confirmation gates or dry-run defaults for destructive operations.
  2. MCP auth friction: Repeated interactive re-auth despite cached refresh tokens (#4203), callback-port mismatches (#4793), and login failures when servers reject a protocol version (#5039) make MCP setup feel brittle — especially in CI and remote workflows.
  3. Windows platform friction: EDR/antivirus interference (#5478), /upgrade bypassing winget and desyncing Add/Remove Programs (#5071), plugin uninstall access-denied errors (#5119), and WSL-only OAuth callback 404s (#4632) form a consistent Windows pain cluster.
  4. Permission fatigue and complexity: Both too many prompts (#5066) and overly complex configuration (#5539) are reported — users want simple, durable rules, not per-repo policy tuning.
  5. Session fragility and UX resets: Unreclaimable locks (#4805), context loss at max_output_tokens (#4733), permission prompts resetting in-progress question dialogs (#5536), and disappearing /ask answers (#4803) all erode session continuity.
  6. Silent failures: Ignored plugin instruction files (#5440), empty MCP text/plain blobs (#4916), and secrets not reaching spawned MCP processes (#4985) are hard to diagnose because nothing surfaces an error.

  • Windows is the sharpest edge. Long command truncation (#12340), missing SIGHUP-equivalent shutdown cleanup (#11889), and install-script confusion with Ubuntu's unrelated pi package (#12166) form a recurring cluster of platform friction.
  • Silent failures erode trust. Truncated-but-"successful" commands (#12340), dropped SSE error codes before retry classification (#12169), and underreported cost tiers (#12308) all share a pattern: wrong behavior with no signal to the developer.
  • Post-1.6.0 reasoning regressions. #12361 and #12367 arriving within 24h of release suggest the codex supportsMidConvoEffort change needs a more careful rollout or per-level validation.
  • OAuth and enterprise auth fragility. Anthropic Team/Enterprise scope rejection (#12318) plus the community OAuth shim (#12364) indicate auth paths need clearer error surfaces and broader seat-type coverage.
  • TUI terminal-state robustness. ANSI paste corruption and editor deadlock (#11383) and theme-contrast readability (#12347) remain persistent papercuts in pi-tui.
  • Long-session scale. The 120k-entry RangeError (#12154) and quadratic catalog merge (#12311) show the codebase needs more stress testing at realistic session and catalog sizes.
Qwen Code — QwenLM/qwen-code

Qwen Code Community Digest — 2026-11-21

1. Today's Highlights

A patch release (v0.28.3) plus a preview and nightly landed, all carrying the same managed-agent E2E and PR-verification hardening work. CI reliability remains the dominant theme: the long-running Managed Agent gate failure (#14724, now 506 comments) and a fresh E2E flake (#17934) drove most activity. Meanwhile, the managed-agent runtime and Web Shell migration continued to advance through a steady stream of stacked PRs.

2. Releases

Three builds published in the last 24h, all sharing an identical change set:

  • v0.28.3 (stable) — release
  • v0.28.1-preview.1 — release
  • v0.28.0-nightly.20261120.19b31401f5 — release

Common changes:

  • test(managed-agent): observe a real scheduled /loop fire in the full-stack E2E (#17506) by @wenshao
  • fix(verify-pr): harden the watch-state shell logic

This is a test/CI hardening release rather than a user-facing feature drop — the notable signal is the team investing in real E2E coverage for the managed-agent scheduler before the 0.28 line stabilizes.

3. Hot Issues

  1. #14724 — Main CI failed: Managed Agent gate, no test identified. 506 comments, open since 2026-10-19. The single most active thread in the repo; a chronic gate that keeps re-firing per commit. Community reaction: near-total bot churn, but it signals a systemic CI stability problem.
  2. #11680 — Main CI failed: E2E Tests (sandbox:docker shard). 100 comments, open since September. A long-lived sandbox E2E failure that never closed — evidence the docker sandbox lane is a persistent weak point.
  3. #15486 — P1 bug: after automatic compaction, the next request double-counts the pending tool result and adds a 20K pad, forcing max_tokens: 1 or a stopped turn. The most substantive correctness bug on the board — directly affects token management and turn success.
  4. #17039 — ci: make the Managed Agent gate name stable so it can become a required check. Root-cause analysis of why a broken Java suite merged via #17006. Now closed/ready-for-human — good sign the gate instability is being addressed at the source.
  5. #16832 — Manual PR re-review channel dead because qwen-code-pr-review.yml gates on a bot account that no longer exists (404). Closed. Notable because it broke re-review repo-wide.
  6. #17523 — managed-agent: pre-admission load refusals still consume the ordinary retry budget. A correctness issue in session load/retry semantics; P2.
  7. #17885 — Windows Java lane red since #17478: a 32,780-char capture payload passed through argv exceeds the Windows 32,767 limit. Sharp, well-diagnosed platform bug; closed.
  8. #17934 — E2E: qwen-serve-restart-recovery fails after daemon SIGKILL. Fresh (created 2026-11-20), 14 comments — the newest reliability regression.
  9. #17957 — Managed Agent gate: RuntimeProviderPluginsTest.builtinProvidersAreTrulyOptionalOnTheApplicationClasspath. Another per-commit gate failure — reinforces the pattern of #14724.
  10. #17086 — qwen4-max-preview: server-side Chinese tool-URL rule (routify) leaks into context and the model flags it as prompt injection. Closed but a genuinely interesting model-behavior/context-hygiene case.

Also worth noting: #17188 (DeepSeek V3.1/V3.2 fall back to the generic 32K output limit despite catalog listing 65536) and #17963 (Web Shell environment panel hidden behind the pending-question card, unscrollable).

4. Key PR Progress

  1. #17965 / #17964 — fix(managed-agent): create the ephemeral Runtime state directory at spawn time, not at provider creation. Restores the rule that constructing a Runtime provider must not touch the filesystem. Two competing implementations from @yiliang114 and @wenshao.
  2. #17953 — feat(managed-agent): runtime-owned background observation (Phase 3b slice 1 + staging schema). Moves running-output digest out of the Harness process so a Harness restart doesn't lose background Shell/Monitor state.
  3. #17474 — feat(managed-agent): wire external foreground Shell into Broker and Control Plane [17357 B/2]. Broker dispatch/cancel/reconcile/close fences plus Control Plane profile negotiation; stacked on #17472.
  4. #17910 — fix(core): retain oversized transcript indexes in a bounded cache class (256 MiB LRU) instead of refusing admission under the shared 64 MiB budget. Directly relevant to large-session performance.
  5. #17952 — feat(web-shell): contract-driven ChatSurface chat column. Backend-neutral renderer for the unified chat surface migration — a key step in the Web Shell refactor.
  6. #17902 — fix(core): correct usage token accounting across the dashboard and /stats, sourcing from the per-request usage ledger instead of session summaries that replay resumed history.
  7. #17951 — fix(release): resume a partial release instead of refusing its retry. Compares the regenerated tree against the existing release branch tip so a partial npm publish can continue.
  8. #17903 — fix(ci): gate the Teams channel on its npm publishing bootstrap, holding it out of release until a maintainer does the one-time public publish.
  9. #17823 — fix(agents): keep A2A tasks recoverable after transcript read errors; returns retryable -32012 instead of losing task results.
  10. #17437 — feat(i18n): Arabic support for CLI and Web Shell with RTL layout, including exported HTML transcripts. Largest user-facing localization addition in the window.

Other notable: #17968 (strengthen four managed DingTalk witnesses that passed for the wrong reason), #17918 (touch acceptance for Web Shell follow-up suggestions), #17935 (dark-theme sidebar logo).

5. Hot Discussions

No GitHub Discussions data was provided for this window; this section is omitted.

6. Feature Request Trends

Distilled from issues and PRs active in the last 24h:

  • Managed-agent runtime maturity — the largest cluster: runtime-owned background observation (#17953), external foreground Shell into Broker/Control Plane (#17474), ephemeral state directory handling (#17964/#17965), and retry-budget correctness (#17523). The managed-agent server is clearly the active development frontier.
  • Session/context management — transcript index retention (#17910), token accounting (#17902), worktree Codex parity P6/P7 (#17237), and JSONL append diagnostics (#17852).
  • Web Shell unification — the shared ChatSurface migration (#17952), worktree parity, touch-suggestion UX (#17918), and UI layout fixes (#17963).
  • Internationalization — Arabic/RTL (#17437) joins the shipped language set.
  • Historical statistics — native /stats activity and efficiency view (#17376).
  • Channel integrations — DingTalk, Teams, QQ, Aone follow-up trackers dominate the integration backlog.

7. Developer Pain Points

  • Chronic CI gate instability — #14724 (506 comments) and the recurring "no test identified" per-commit failures (#11680, #11678, #13471, #17957) are the top frustration. The gate name being unstable blocked it from becoming a required check (#17039), and a broken Java suite merged via #17006, poisoning subsequent PRs.
  • Broken tooling infrastructure — the PR re-review channel silently died because it referenced a deleted bot account (#16832), a 404-level breakage of maintainer workflow.
  • Platform-specific failures — the Windows argv 32,767-char limit (#17885) and macOS/docker E2E lanes produce deterministic, hard-to-triage red lanes.
  • Token/context accounting bugs — double-counting after compaction (#15486) and model output-limit normalization (DeepSeek #17188) cause real user-visible turn failures.
  • Flaky tests — repeated deflake issues (e.g., #17884) show nondeterministic tests consuming review cycles.
  • Process overhead — many issues are "follow-up trackers" for deferred non-blocking review suggestions (#17173, #17517, #17673, #17769, #17924, #17931), suggesting a heavy review-convergence process that defers rather than resolves items.

item.content:encoded:
OpenClaw Ecosystem Digest 2026-11-21

Issues: 333 | PRs: 500 | Projects covered: 5 | Generated: 2026-11-21 02:06 UTC

  • OpenClaw
  • Hermes Agent
  • IronClaw
  • QwenPaw
  • ZeroClaw

OpenClaw Deep Dive

OpenClaw Project Digest — 2026-11-21

1. Today's Overview

OpenClaw shows very high maintenance activity but a troubled stability posture on 2026-11-21: 333 issues were updated in the last 24 hours (245 still active) and 500 PRs were touched (305 still open). No new releases shipped, and the absence of a release while P0/P1 crash-loop and release-blocker issues remain open suggests the project is in a stabilization phase rather than a shipping phase. Activity is overwhelmingly concentrated in bug triage and reliability work — particularly around the managed-update pipeline, Gateway startup performance, plugin preparation stalls, and prompt-cache regressions. The signal-to-noise ratio is concerning: a large share of the top-commented issues are regressions introduced between 2026.9.x and 2026.11.x, indicating that recent feature velocity is outpacing regression coverage. Encouragingly, several fix PRs are in flight (#202815, #202834, #202836, #202837, #202846) and a handful of stale/closed issues (#120385, #162914, #185064, #186326, #202246) resolved today, showing the triage pipeline is not stalled.

2. Releases

No new releases in the last 24 hours. The most recent referenced versions in active reports are 2026.11.5 (stable candidate), 2026.11.5-beta.4, and 2026.11.6 (referenced in a closed Discord duplicate-message issue). No changelog, breaking-change, or migration notes are available today. Maintainers should be aware that there is a substantial backlog of update-pipeline blockers (see §5) gating the next stable cut.

3. Project Progress

While no releases landed, 195 PRs were merged or closed in the last 24 hours (out of 500 total updated). Notable closed issues include:

  • [CLOSED] #120385 — Code Mode tool catalog incomplete for scheduled/cron turns (stale, superseded by author correction). Link
  • [CLOSED] #162914 — Intermittent Aborted | sandbox_provisioning failures with rootless Podman sandbox. Link
  • [CLOSED] #185064 — GPT-6.1 Terra route/auth preparation failures (linked PR open). Link
  • [CLOSED] #186326 — Windows managed update SQLite file-lock timeout after npm layout repair. Link
  • [CLOSED] #202246 — 2026.11.6 goal-continuation prompts producing duplicate Discord reminders (P1, message-loss). Link
  • [CLOSED] #195279 — Background exec completion wake failing with "operator execution authority no longer active" (P1, security). Link

Fix PRs advancing today (open, awaiting review):

  • #202815 — stop recursive Git shims from exhausting agent sandboxes (sandbox stability). Link
  • #202834 — shorten WAL pins during cold transcript archival (DB performance). Link
  • #202836 — keep valid SQLite opens available after failed requests. Link
  • #202837 — release completed lease callers and keep input tests portable. Link
  • #202846 — preserve RFB cancellation and portable test ownership. Link
  • #201503 — tell hooks which turn started the command a completion run reports. Link
  • #202689 — keep dismissed automation failures out of the Inbox. Link
  • #196092 — store every reply in chat history for claude-cli backend. Link

4. Community Hot Topics

Ranked by comment count, the following issues dominate maintainer and community attention:

# Issue Comments Signal
1 #160959 — Gateway blocks for minutes on large external plugins (2026.9.6 regression) 84 🔴 P0, crash-loop, diamond lobster
2 #191944 — macOS gateway stop/stop --force both fail 38 P2, UX friction, stable
3 #197083 — Post-install Doctor WAL publication leaves 11.3 partially finalized 31 🔴 P0, release-blocker
4 #178359 — doctor --fix --non-interactive hangs 15+ min 31 🟠 P1, crash-loop
5 #168955 — Startup regression 1030s vs 410s (Windows) 23 🟠 P1, crash-loop
6 #182891 — Prompt cache never reused (cache read dropped N -> 0) 20 P2, behavior
7 #200606 — 2026.11.5 candidate Doctor blocks update with changed=[] 19 🟠 P1
8 #153899 — Gateway drain waits full TimeoutStopSec 11 🟠 P1, crash-loop
9 #198218 — Doctor/update maintenance livelocks (platinum hermit) 11 🟠 P1, crash-loop
10 #155868 — Agent-sourced runs get reduced tool roster → prompt-cache miss 11 P2, security review

Underlying needs analysis:

  • Update reliability is the #1 theme. Six of the top-10 issues involve openclaw update, doctor --fix, WAL publication, or candidate validation (#197083, #178359, #200606, #198218, plus closed #186326). Users are clearly hitting managed-update failures across platforms (macOS, Windows, WSL2, Linux) and are losing trust in the upgrade path.
  • Startup/plugin performance is the #2 theme. #160959, #168955, #174681, #187350 all describe Gateway startup or main-thread stalls of minutes to over 1000 seconds. The plugin-generation capture feature (#144252) is a recurring root cause.
  • Prompt-cache economics (#182891, #198373, #155868) matters to power users paying per-token; cache-read collapsing to ~0–3% has real cost impact.

5. Bugs & Stability

Ranked by severity (P0 → P2), with fix status noted:

🔴 P0 / Release-Blockers

  • #160959 — Gateway event loop blocked for minutes capturing large external plugins (2026.9.6 regression, first shipped #144252). 84 comments, no new fix PR, needs maintainer review. Highest-impact open bug.
  • #197083 — Post-install Doctor WAL publication verification fails, leaving 11.3 partially finalized with external plugin breakage. UX release-blocker. [Fix shape clear but no new PR.]
  • #158277 — Talk on Watch (Apple Watch) fails with "Voice changed its remote network address." P0 / UX release-blocker, 7 comments.

🟠 P1 / Crash-Loop

  • #178359 — doctor --fix --non-interactive idles 15+ min, never reaches DB repair.
  • #168955 — Windows startup regression: ready ~1030s vs ~410s; sidecars.control-ui-assets blocks 477s.
  • #168955, #153899 (Gateway drain waits full TimeoutStopSec), #198218 (Doctor/update livelock), #197515 (Codex "data/settings upgrade unfinished" — merged fix #186506 not in release), #192524 (scheduled agentTurn refused through aws-sdk provider).
  • #174681 — Regression: #172750 plugin preparation blocks Gateway main thread (fix already reverted on release branch). Mitigation exists.

🟡 P2 / Regressions & Behavior

  • #182891 & #198373 — Prompt-cache never reused / history rewritten between turns (OpenAI-compatible routes). Cost impact.
  • #200606 — Candidate Doctor blocks 2026.11.3 → 2026.11.5 with changed=[].
  • #200756 / #200610 — Windows beta.2 → beta.4 update fails at package-swap; retained updater runtime paths exceed MAX_PATH and can't be deleted.
  • #200224 — 2026.11.5 beta refuses retired agents.defaults.heartbeat, but removing it re-enables heartbeats (catch-22).
  • #177989 — Kimi Code repeats tool calls / over-polls background processes.
  • #162448 — Linux desktop app minimize/maximize/close buttons overlap side panel (has clawsweeper:queueable-fix).
  • #192496 — Idle skills refresh still re-enters at 19–20 agents (symptom persists after PR #170341).

Fix-PR availability: Only a minor fraction of the top bugs have active fix PRs. The update-pipeline cluster (#197083, #200606, #200756, #200610) appears to need maintainer-level product decisions, not just code fixes — a risk for the next release.

6. Feature Requests & Roadmap Signals

Active feature requests updated today, with roadmap prediction:

Issue Feature Likelihood in next version
#197297 Per-user secret vault for multi-user Gateways Medium — needs security review, narrow core + plugin design proposed
#187264 Caller-scoped, same-conversation scheduling for non-owner channel requests Medium — Slack use case, security review flagged
#178373 Run-level turn/token budget + default-on tool-loop detection Medium-High — addresses runaway cost; config default change is low-risk
#131457 (CLOSED) Feishu (Lark) progress streaming mode Low near-term — closed as stale, but parity request is durable
#130247 Cron --until / --max-runs + cumulative run counter Medium — small, bounded scope
#170261 Matrix: deliver final reply as new message when streaming Medium — search discoverability fix
#179685 IMAP durable processing handoff + inspectable outcomes Low-Medium — opt-in reliability extension
#181791 Durable owner-native execution provenance for safe interruption recovery Low near-term — architectural, Control Centre integration
#181579 Better progress narration grounding Low — UX polish

Prediction: The most likely near-term shipped features are tool-loop budget defaults (#178373) and cron end conditions (#130247), since both are bounded and address cost/ops pain. The per-user vault (#197297) and caller-scoped scheduling (#187264) are strategically important but gated on security review.

7. User Feedback Summary

Pain points (dissatisfaction):

  1. Update pipeline is the dominant source of frustration. Users on macOS, Windows 11, WSL2, and Linux all report managed updates failing, hanging, or leaving partially-finalized state (#197083, #178359, #200606, #200756, #200610, #198218). One user reported a single update window taking 5409 seconds (#201251).
  2. Startup has regressed materially — #168955 reports Windows ready time ~1030s vs ~410s prior; #187350 reports 58s per startup in plugin metadata rescan on Docker/NAS.
  3. Gateway unresponsiveness during plugin work (#160959, #174681) — a minutes-long event-loop block is unacceptable for a personal assistant product.
  4. Cost leakage via prompt-cache failure (#182891, #198373) — power users on OpenAI-compatible providers see cache-read collapse to 1–3%.
  5. Cross-platform polish gaps — Linux desktop overlapping window controls (#162448), macOS gateway stop failing (#191944), iOS text-size control not working (#170428, closed), Android setup stuck on approval (#201489).

Satisfaction signals:

  • Users are engaged and providing detailed, high-quality reproducers (e.g., #198218 reproduced on two versions, #201251 with exact timings). This is a technically sophisticated, deeply invested user base.
  • The "diamond lobster" / "platinum hermit" issue-rating taxonomy shows a mature triage culture.
  • Some fixes are landing and appreciated (closed #162914, #185064, #195279).

Net sentiment: Frustration is concentrated on the update and startup experience, not the core agent capability. Users clearly love the product enough to file 333 issues in 24 hours — but trust in shipping quality is eroding.

8. Backlog Watch

Long-unanswered or high-value issues/PRs needing maintainer attention:

Item Age Why it matters
#160959 Created 2026-09-29 (~7.5 weeks), 84 comments Highest-comment P0; no new fix PR; still open. Top backlog priority.
#153899 Created 2026-09-20 (~9 weeks), 11 comments Stale-flagged P1 crash-loop; Gateway drain waits full stop window. Needs maintainer review.
#155868 Created 2026-09-22 (~9 weeks), 11 comments Tool-roster mismatch → prompt-cache miss; flagged needs-security-review.
#178373 Created 2026-10-20 (~4.5 weeks), 11 comments Runaway-cost guardrails; needs product decision.
#138528 Created 2026-09-04 (~11 weeks), 9 comments Stuck-session recovery discards blocked_tool_call cause; stale but fix-shape-clear.
#130247 Created 2026-08-26 (~13 weeks), 10 comments Cron has no end conditions; long-standing, small scope.
#167622 Created 2026-10-09 (~6 weeks), 10 comments

Cross-Ecosystem Comparison

Cross-Project Comparison Report — Personal AI Assistant / Agent Open-Source Ecosystem

Date: 2026-11-21 | Projects analyzed: OpenClaw, Hermes Agent, IronClaw, QwenPaw, ZeroClaw

1. Ecosystem Overview

The personal AI assistant / agent open-source landscape on 2026-11-21 is characterized by intense maintenance activity across a maturing, multi-front ecosystem. Five projects were tracked; four showed high or very high activity, while one (IronClaw) was dormant. The dominant narrative is a shift from feature velocity to stabilization and reliability hardening — every active project is fighting regressions introduced by recent feature pushes (update pipelines, session-state durability, channel reliability, prompt-cache economics). A second clear theme is infrastructure deepening: local model management, credential/OAuth scoping, plugin APIs, and storage abstractions are being built out in parallel across projects. Community contribution pipelines are generally healthy, but review throughput and a few structural blockers (notably Hermes' upstream PR-permission bug and ZeroClaw's stalled merge queue) are emerging as the ecosystem's primary bottlenecks.

2. Activity Comparison

Project Issues Updated (24h) Open Issues PRs Updated (24h) PRs Open Merged/Closed Release Status Health Score
OpenClaw 333 (245 active) 245 500 305 195 None (stabilization) 🟡 6.5/10
Hermes Agent 50 39 50 44 6 Canary v0.23.3 🟢 7.5/10
IronClaw 0 — 0 — 0 None ⚪ N/A (dormant)
QwenPaw 16 ~16 47 29 18 None (post-v2.3.0.post1) 🟢 7.5/10
ZeroClaw 12 12 49 48 1 None 🟡 6/10

Notes on scoring methodology: Health scores weigh (a) merge throughput relative to intake, (b) severity of open P0/P1 bugs, (c) release cadence, and (d) community responsiveness. OpenClaw scores lower despite the highest raw activity because of its release-blocker backlog and low fix-PR coverage on top bugs. ZeroClaw is penalized for a near-stalled merge queue. Hermes and QwenPaw are balanced despite different sizes.

3. OpenClaw's Position

Advantages vs. peers:

  • Scale of community: OpenClaw is an order of magnitude larger than any peer — 333 issues and 500 PRs updated in a single day vs. ~50 for Hermes and ZeroClaw. This is a genuinely large, technically sophisticated contributor base producing high-quality reproducers (e.g., #198218 reproduced on two versions).
  • Mature triage culture: The "diamond lobster" / "platinum hermit" issue-rating taxonomy indicates an established severity discipline that smaller projects lack.
  • Broadest platform surface: Cross-platform coverage (macOS, Windows, WSL2, Linux, iOS, Android, Apple Watch) exceeds all peers, with correspondingly more integration surface.

Disadvantages vs. peers:

  • Lowest fix-PR coverage on top bugs. Only a minority of OpenClaw's top-10 issues have active fix PRs; Hermes and QwenPaw routinely ship same-day fix PRs for P2 bugs. OpenClaw's top P0 (#160959) has been open ~7.5 weeks with no new fix PR.
  • No release in the window while release-blockers remain open — a shipping-confidence gap that peers avoid through frequent canary cuts (Hermes) or rapid patch PRs (QwenPaw).
  • Feature velocity outpacing regression coverage, evidenced by a large share of top issues being 2026.9.x → 2026.11.x regressions.

Technical approach differences: OpenClaw runs the heaviest, most architecturally complex stack of the group — managed-update pipeline with WAL publication, plugin-generation capture, sandbox provisioning (rootless Podman), and a Gateway event loop that several bugs show is vulnerable to multi-minute stalls. Peers favor lighter, more modular architectures: QwenPaw is extracting local model management into a Plugin Provider (PR #8499) and Hermes is building a storage abstraction layer (PR #149566). OpenClaw's breadth buys capability but creates the very coupling (plugin prep → main-thread block) driving its top bugs.

Community size comparison: OpenClaw ≈ 6–7× Hermes Agent and ≈ 7× ZeroClaw in daily issue/PR volume; ≈ 20× QwenPaw in issue intake. It is the de facto reference implementation but also carries the largest maintenance debt.

4. Shared Technical Focus Areas

The following requirements are emerging independently across multiple projects, indicating ecosystem-level pain points rather than project-specific defects:

Shared Requirement OpenClaw Hermes QwenPaw ZeroClaw Specific Need
Session/state durability #197083 (partial finalization) #107149, #156335, #134290 (lock files, orphaned writers, vanishing turns) #8580 (memory index never rebuilds) #8794 (mid-work stop erases context), #12607 (memory contradiction) Durable, self-healing session/transcript storage with no silent loss
Silent-failure observability #160959 (event-loop block, no signal) — #8757, #8580, #8123 (health OK while broken) #12597 (Telegram offset stall) Subsystems must surface failure + auto-recover, not report "healthy"
Update/install reliability #197083, #178359, #200606, #200756 (macOS/Windows/WSL2/Linux) #158266 (Docker module missing), #155862 (first-run stall) Windows file-lock races (#8835) — Cross-platform managed-update must be atomic and reversible
Credential/OAuth scoping #197297 (per-user vault) #149642, #152732, PR #156606 — #12422 (RFC), #12596 (browser grants) Security-grade, scoped credential handling for multi-user/service auth
Local inference management — #158383 (llama.cpp provider bug) #8649/#8647/#8648 (GPU, MLX, auto-update) — First-class local model lifecycle (download, GPU, update)
Prompt-cache economics #182891, #198373, #155868 (cache-read → 1–3%) — — — Cache reuse correctness directly tied to per-token cost
Channel reliability (messaging) Discord dup (#202246) Feishu drops (#31336), LINE files (#155992) WeChat polling death (#8757) Telegram (#12597), WhatsApp (#12598) Per-channel edge-case correctness and retry

The two strongest cross-cutting signals are (1) session/state durability and (2) silent-failure observability — appearing in four and three projects respectively. These are the ecosystem's most urgent shared technical debts.

5. Differentiation Analysis

Dimension OpenClaw Hermes Agent QwenPaw ZeroClaw
Feature focus Full-stack assistant platform; managed updates, plugins, multi-channel Plugin/credential infra, governance, storage abstraction Local inference, Console UX, Office skills Channel reliability, memory quality, security/identity
Target users Power users, cross-platform personal assistant operators Contributors, plugin developers, production/VPS operators Desktop + mobile local-model users Group-chat operators, service-auth users
Architecture Heavy, tightly-coupled Gateway + plugin-generation capture + WAL update pipeline Modular, storage-abstraction-in-progress, canary rolling releases Plugin-Provider extraction, Console-centric RFC/ADR-driven identity-access, WASM sandbox
Release rhythm Slow, stabilization-gated Frequent canary Post-rollout patching Stalled merge queue
Distinctive bet Breadth + ecosystem scale Plugin/credential security depth Local inference as first-class Security-grade identity (OIDC/ADR)
Notable weakness Regression coverage Upstream PR-permission blocker (#131859) Responsive-UI regressions Merge throughput (48 open PRs)

Key differentiators: OpenClaw competes on breadth and ecosystem gravity; Hermes on security/plugin infrastructure depth; QwenPaw on local-inference ownership; ZeroClaw on identity/security architecture. Notably, none of the four is converging on the same feature set — they occupy complementary niches, which reduces direct head-to-head competition but also means users may combine projects (e.g., ZeroClaw's credential model with QwenPaw's local runtime).

6. Community Momentum & Maturity

Activity tiers:

  • Tier 1 (very high, at scale): OpenClaw — 333 issues + 500 PRs/24h. Massive but strained.
  • Tier 2 (high, balanced): Hermes Agent and QwenPaw — ~50–63 combined items/24h, with strong same-day fix-PR velocity.
  • Tier 3 (moderate, bottlenecked): ZeroClaw — 61 items/24h but 1 merge; contributor supply outpaces review.
  • Dormant: IronClaw — no activity.

Rapidly iterating vs. stabilizing:

  • Rapidly iterating: ZeroClaw (new bug intake 7/12 filed yesterday; RFC/ADR design work) and QwenPaw (stacked local-model PR set, 18 PRs merged today).
  • Stabilizing: OpenClaw (explicit stabilization phase, no release, regression triage) and Hermes (canary cadence, foundational storage refactor, P2 fix cadence).
  • Blocked: ZeroClaw's merge throughput and Hermes' external contribution pipeline (#131859, 7 weeks) are the two clearest momentum inhibitors.

Maturity signals: All four active projects exhibit professional-grade hygiene — severity taxonomies, RFC/ADR processes, ci-reviewed tags, credential redaction (QwenPaw #8790), and detailed repro culture. Hermes and QwenPaw show the healthiest responsiveness-to-activity ratio; OpenClaw shows the largest absolute engagement but weakest shipping confidence; ZeroClaw shows strong design ambition but review bandwidth constraints.

7. Trend Signals

Signals extracted from community feedback across all projects, with implications for AI agent developers:

  1. Reliability is the new differentiator — not capability. Every active project's top pain points are regressions, not missing features. Implication: ship regression coverage (golden-path tests for update, startup, session persistence) alongside features; treat reliability as a first-class product surface.

  2. "Silent failure" is the most trust-destroying bug class. Memory indexes, channel pollers, and update pipelines all report healthy while broken (QwenPaw #8757/#8580, ZeroClaw #12597, OpenClaw #160959). Implication: build health signals that are causal (did the subsystem actually do its job?) rather than liveness-only (is the process up?).

  3. Session-state durability is table stakes for an "assistant." Vanishing turns, orphaned writers, and permanent lock files (Hermes, ZeroClaw, OpenClaw) directly undermine the memory/transcript value proposition. Implication: invest early in a durable, crash-safe storage layer (Hermes' SQLite abstraction is the model to watch).

  4. Update/install is the #1 source of churn. OpenClaw and Hermes both show cross-platform managed-update failures dominating frustration. Implication: make updates atomic, resumable, and observable; a broken updater erodes trust faster than any missing feature.

  5. Credential and OAuth scoping is the next infrastructure frontier. Independently emerging in OpenClaw, Hermes, and ZeroClaw. Implication: design for multi-user, per-scope credentials and exact-match OAuth redirects now — plugin ecosystems will demand it.

  6. Local inference is becoming a first-class concern. QwenPaw's GPU/MLX/auto-update stack and Hermes' llama.cpp issues signal that local model lifecycle management is moving from "nice to have" to expected. Implication: abstract the runtime so local and cloud backends share a provider interface.

  7. Prompt-cache economics matter to power users. OpenClaw's cache-read collapse (1–3%) has direct cost impact. Implication: treat cache reuse correctness as a correctness bug, not an optimization.

  8. Review throughput, not contributor supply, is the ecosystem's constraint. ZeroClaw (48 open PRs, 1 merge) and Hermes (44/50 open) show intake outpacing merge capacity. Implication: projects that invest in triage/merge automation and clear contributor blockers (Hermes #131859) will convert community energy into shipped value faster than those that don't.

Notable: two S1 "workflow blocked" bugs are open, and the oldest (#8794) has been unresolved since July — a stability concern. Only the S2 MCP duplication bug has a corresponding fix PR today. A security-relevant dependency issue (RUSTSEC-2026-0587) has a fix PR #12610 pending.

6. Feature Requests & Roadmap Signals

  • #12614 — Browser tool lacks a file-upload action, blocking any form requiring attachment. The wrapped agent-browser CLI already supports upload, so this is a low-friction gap likely to land soon.
  • #12598 — WhatsApp Web: send replies as quoted replies so group members know who was answered (mentions currently broken per #10976).
  • #12022 — External rerank stage for memory (in-progress).
  • #12611 / PR #12612 — Retire local LLM response cache.
  • #12613 — "Deslop" cleanup tracker: dead code, inert features, comment/docs cruft.

Prediction for next version: the response-cache retirement (breaking), the MCP double-delivery fix, and the wasmtime security bump are the closest to merge-ready. Browser file-upload and Telegram offset fix are likely near-term candidates given clear scope. Credential-scoping/OIDC work is larger and likely lands across multiple releases.

7. User Feedback Summary

  • Pain points: (1) Loss of work — stopping an agent wipes reasoning/tool context (#8794), a serious trust issue for interactive use. (2) Channel reliability — a single failed voice transcription bricks a Telegram channel (#12597), and WhatsApp group replies are ambiguous (#12598). (3) Memory correctness — users report the system both missing saved facts and persisting contradictory versions after correction (#12607), undermining the core memory value proposition.
  • Use cases: Telegram/WhatsApp group assistants, browser automation with authenticated forms, service-to-service auth via operator-managed credentials.
  • Satisfaction signal: users are engaged and constructive (detailed repro timelines, diagnostic details, e.g., #12607), and contributors are investing in RFCs/ADRs — a healthy sign. Dissatisfaction is concentrated on state durability and channel edge cases, not on fundamentals.

8. Backlog Watch

Long-lived items needing maintainer attention:

  • Issue #8794 — Open since 2026-07-07 (~4.5 months), S1, risk:high, status:accepted but no fix PR. Highest-priority backlog item.
  • Issue #12022 — Open since 2026-10-25, in-progress memory rerank; watch for PR.
  • PR #11885 — "fence live policy cutovers," open since 2026-10-19, self-described as "formal final review: FAIL … not a request to merge." XL and stalled.
  • PR #11868 — Open since 2026-10-19, risk:high, depends on #12265; needs-maintainer-review.
  • PR #11076 — Open since 2026-09-23 (~2 months), XL Antigravity CLI tool; long-running.
  • PR #12271 / PR #12376 — Stacked web/Discord work; watch dependency chains.

Health note: with 48 open PRs and near-zero merge throughput today, the review bottleneck — not contributor supply — is the project's primary constraint. Clearing the long-open S1 (#8794) and the stalled XL review queue would materially improve project health.
