  8. #64416 — OVHcloud Qwen3.8-27B fails with missing finish_reason; reporter includes a working workaround. Pattern of non-OpenAI-compliant streaming providers breaking the chat stream parser.
  9. #64494 — Pre-upgrade sessions invisible after V1→V2 upgrade; directory→project resolution ignores imported project records and mints duplicates. Data is intact but effectively lost to users — high-severity migration bug.
  10. #64488 — Context percentage exceeds 100%, using cumulative session tokens rather than live context window. Undermines trust in the context meter; closed same day.

Key PR Progress

  1. #64572 — Fall back to classical TLS handshake when post-quantum ClientHello is dropped (Russian ISPs, Turkish networks). Notable infra robustness fix for a real-world connectivity regression from Bun 1.4.1+.
  2. #64565 — Fixes two desktop timeline renderer crashes (#63944, #62800), including thoughts streamed with no readable text. High-impact stability patch.
  3. #64437 — Embeddable Rust port of Code Mode (psychoscript crate), running without Bun/Node. Signals serious investment in Code Mode as an embeddable primitive.
  4. #64515 — Tool selection and Code Mode placement now derived from the session's model in SessionContext.select. Architectural consolidation of model-aware tooling.
  5. #64546 — Durable video jobs that survive server restarts; groundwork for the agent video tool (#63666).
  6. #63002 — Signed-in browser pane with extensions, previews, cookie/sign-in import from 14+ browsers, and agent safeguards. Large desktop feature under active review.
  7. #61728 — Configurable compaction window (tokens) for automatic compaction planning. Addresses the compaction-crash class of issues (#64500).
  8. #64545 — Wrap long lines in timeline code blocks, with global setting and per-block override. Direct fix for #60143.
  9. #64554 — Fall back when the configured compaction model's provider is unreachable. Prevents hard failures in long sessions.
  10. #58091 — TUI locale truncation by display width (fixes emoji splitting / CJK under-truncation, #58085). Long-standing i18n correctness fix now in review.

Feature Request Trends

  • Model catalog freshness: Multiple issues (#40524, #64489, #64507) ask for live reconciliation with provider /models endpoints — stale static catalogs hide newly released and locally-enabled models.
  • Context/compaction control: Configurable compaction windows (#61728), accurate context-percentage reporting (#64488), and visibility into router-chosen upstream models (#60309) show demand for transparency and control over context economics.
  • Verification and trust: #64419 proposes a deterministic "prove done" hook (Countersign integration) — agents verifying real-world outcomes (live URLs, PR state, DNS) with hash-chained receipts.
  • Browser/agent capability expansion: Signed-in browser panes (#63002), passkey handoff to system browser (#64498), and Code Mode file APIs (#64518) point toward richer in-app agent tooling.

Developer Pain Points

  • Desktop renderer fragility: Three separate crash/fatal-error reports (#63944, #62800, plus the model-picker stutter #64570) erode confidence in the Electron desktop app, especially on Windows and macOS.
  • V1→V2 migration fallout: Sessions disappearing after upgrade (#64494), plugin incompatibility (v1.19.6 notes), and repeated auth-scope errors (#61342) make upgrades feel risky.
  • Provider ecosystem edge cases: Non-compliant streaming (missing finish_reason, #64416), empty tool-call persistence (#64481), and uncached GPT-6.2 instructions (#64550) show that provider-specific behavior remains the top source of breakage.
  • CJK/i18n rendering: Wrong glyphs (#64543), display-width truncation (#58085, #64538), and inconsistent width calculation form a recurring cluster affecting non-Latin-script users.
  • Opaque background operations: SSH setup progress (#56668) and service-start failures (#54059) surface as frozen dialogs or misleading errors, forcing guesswork.
Pi — earendil-works/pi

Pi Community Digest — 2026-11-18

1. Today's Highlights

No new releases in the last 24h, but the issue tracker is highly active with 38 issues updated. A notable cluster of p0/abort-related crashes (codemode tools.read() cancellation) is being triaged and closed rapidly, while Windows support and a persistent npm search indexing problem for pi-package discovery continue to dominate community attention. A long-running context-window discrepancy with gpt-6.1-sol via ChatGPT sign-in also drew the most upvotes today.

2. Releases

No new releases in the last 24h.

3. Hot Issues

  1. #7547 [OPEN] How do you use Pi on Windows? — 97 comments, the most-discussed issue in the tracker. A long-running meta-thread on Windows support fragmentation (WSL, native, Git Bash, etc.). Still open since August; signals that Windows onboarding remains a major community concern.

  2. #11021 [OPEN] ChatGPT sign-in reports 272K for GPT-6.1 Sol despite 500K catalog — 15 comments, 8 👍 (highest upvote count shown). Context/compaction budget mismatch between Pi and the server-advertised window. High user impact for anyone on ChatGPT auth; active discussion of how model catalogs are resolved.

  3. #7885 [CLOSED] npm search not indexing newly published pi-packages — 17 comments. Newly published packages with the pi-package keyword never appear in npm search, breaking the pi.dev/packages gallery mirroring. Closed, but related issue #6873 remains a recurring theme.

  4. #11460 [CLOSED, p0, fix-available] Resume drops all built-in tools when session branch is truncated — 6 comments. Orphan parentId after ENOSPC causes session resume to lose defaultTools. A serious data-integrity/resume bug; fix is available, good sign for the p0 pipeline.

  5. #11956 [CLOSED, p0] Crash on cancelling a read during file open — 7 comments. Uncaught AbortError crashes the process when a read tool call is cancelled mid-open (e.g., in codemode Promise.all). Part of a cluster of related abort crashes (see #12271, #12253).

  6. #12266 [CLOSED] Idle second Pi instance appends with stale leaf, forking session tree — 5 comments. Two processes on the same session file cause sibling-branch forking; resume lands on the empty branch. Concurrency-safety concern for multi-instance workflows.

  7. #12096 [OPEN] /login llama.cpp connection store doesn't persist across sessions — 5 comments. Local-model users lose their llama.cpp connection config between sessions. Persistent-state bug affecting the local inference crowd.

  8. #12070 [OPEN] pi-ai: wire stream timeoutMs on google-vertex and classify mid-stream resets as retryable — 4 comments. Stalled/reset Vertex streams hang indefinitely or fail without retry. Reliability gap for evaluation harnesses on GCP.

  9. #12184 [CLOSED] Google adapters reject Gemini 4 Hydrogen's advertised xhigh level (dup of #12177, 2 👍) — 4 comments. New Gemini 4 Hydrogen features are advertised but throw before any HTTP request. Model-capability drift between models.dev metadata and adapters.

  10. #12076 [OPEN] Compaction: Pi ends a tool loop silently instead of compacting — 4 comments. Near context limit, Pi loops on compaction attempts and silently terminates the tool loop (reproduced twice on vLLM). High-severity agent-flow issue; likely related to the larger compaction thread below.

4. Key PR Progress

  1. #12028 [OPEN] fix(coding-agent): defer sendMessage triggerTurn until compaction ends — Closes #10982. Prevents sendMessage({triggerTurn: true}) from starting a run on the uncompacted branch while manual compaction is in progress. Important correctness fix for extension authors.

  2. #12262 [CLOSED] Emit session_compact for boundary-draft compactions — Fixes missing session_compact events when extensions commit compactions via turn_end / agent_before_settle boundary drafts. Companion to issue #12263; unblocks extension event handling.

  3. #12256 [CLOSED] Fix scoped skill collision diagnostics — Suppresses warnings for intentional higher-precedence skill overrides while keeping warnings for genuinely ambiguous same-precedence collisions. Reduces warning noise.

  4. #12249 [CLOSED] feat(ai): record ttftMs and ttfaMs on streamed assistant messages — Adds first-token and first-any-payload latency to AssistantMessage, extending the existing durationMs metric. Useful for benchmarking and provider comparisons.

  5. Issue-cluster fix activity (no standalone PR visible) — Several abort-related crashes were closed with fixes referenced in-thread: #12271, #12253, and #11956 all converge on codemode cancellation handling. Worth tracking whether a unified fix lands.

Note: Only 4 PRs were updated in the last 24h; the digest includes all of them rather than padding the list.

5. Hot Discussions

No discussion data was provided.

6. Feature Request Trends

  • Provider expansion: Requests for new built-in providers (Sarvam AI Token Factory, #12258/#12255) and better handling of gateway-advertised capabilities like ultra thinking tiers (#12267) and Gemini xhigh (#12184).
  • Thinking-level / cache preservation: Keep prompt cache when changing thinking level mid-conversation (#12269).
  • Extension/event surface: Emit session_compact consistently for boundary-draft compactions (#12263).
  • UX polish: Clickable branch name in the footer (#12270); better unknown-argument error messages listing declared parameter names (#12252).
  • Windows ergonomics: Consolidating Windows usage guidance and delegating non-core variants (#7547).

7. Developer Pain Points

  • Windows support fragmentation remains the single largest open discussion; users lack a clear "blessed" path across WSL/native/Git Bash.
  • Package discovery on pi.dev: npm search index lag means new pi-package releases are invisible in browse/search even when detail pages work (#7885, #6873). Recurring since July.
  • Codemode cancellation crashes: Unhandled AbortError during in-flight tools.read() (and sibling tool calls) crashes the whole process (#11956, #12253, #12271) — a concentrated reliability hotspot.
  • Concurrency & shared state: Multiple Pi processes on the same session cause stale-leaf forking (#12266), and concurrent managed npm installs race the shared .pi/npm prefix with no install lock (#10798).
  • Compaction behavior: Silent tool-loop termination near context limits (#12076), and compaction overrides ignored for routed/virtual models (#12265).
  • Provider/metadata drift: Advertised model capabilities (context windows, thinking tiers) not honored by adapters (#11021, #12184, #12177, #12267).
  • Local-model persistence: llama.cpp connection store not surviving session restarts (#12096).
  • Small but sharp terminal bugs: External SIGTSTP leaves terminals in raw mouse-tracking state (#12272); unregistered tool calls never resolve and leak framing to the TUI (#12261).

Methodology note: items were selected from the top-comment issues (top 30 of 38) and all 4 updated PRs, weighted by comment count and 👍. Several closed items are included because they reflect active triage momentum; "CLOSED" status is noted per item.

Qwen Code — QwenLM/qwen-code

Qwen Code Community Digest — 2026-11-18

1. Today's Highlights

Qwen Code shipped v0.28.0 alongside a v0.28.1-preview.0 patch, the TypeScript SDK v0.1.35, and Qwen Code Desktop v0.28.0, headlined by the new Web Shell sidebar workspace filter and the managed DingTalk adapter. Meanwhile, the community's attention is dominated by the 1.0 Preview loop kernel migration (#17045) and a broad cluster of Java SDK correctness bugs filed in a single day. CI reliability remains a persistent theme, with the long-running Managed Agent gate failure (#14724) now at 431 comments.

2. Releases

  • v0.28.1-preview.0 — Preview patch; adds a full-stack E2E test observing a real scheduled /loop fire in the managed-agent path, plus hardening of the verify-pr watcher.
  • v0.28.0 — Stable release with no known breaking changes. Features include the Web Shell sidebar workspace filter (#17244) and managed-agent DingTalk adapter work.
  • sdk-typescript-v0.1.35 — Bundles CLI 0.28.0 (built from the same source ref as the SDK). Note the release notes also reference a 0.27.4 bundle lineage.
  • desktop-v0.28.0 — Desktop build tracking 0.28.0, including the sidebar workspace filter and the DingTalk adapter.

3. Hot Issues

  1. #14724 — Main CI failed: Managed Agent gate — no test identified. Open since October 19 with 431 comments; the single largest ongoing thread in the repo and a persistent blocker for CI trustworthiness.
  2. #13078 — Daily dependency CVE audit failed. 55 comments; a recurring automation failure that keeps resurfacing, possibly due to npm audit endpoint availability.
  3. #17045 — tracking(core): land the 1.0 Preview loop kernel on main, one surface at a time. The centerpiece refactor of the current cycle; freeze scheduled for 2026-11-21, so activity is intense.
  4. #13851 — Non-interactive (headless/SDK) mode delays terminal result until managed auto-memory tasks finish. Highlights a 40 s–5 min latency gap versus the TUI/ACP paths — a serious concern for SDK consumers.
  5. #15082 — Managed Agent: define a capacity and idle-reclamation model. Multi-agent roadmap item requesting admission control and documented runtime/memory limits.
  6. #17666 — Make the built-in image_gen tool work with Qwen subscription auth. The Plus plan includes image generation and Qwen Code access, but the tool only registers under certain providers — a clear subscription-value gap.
  7. #15738 — Team mode: teammate messages never delivered to the leader in ACP mode; team dies with the short-lived ACP child. High-impact multi-agent/Web Shell defect for qwen serve --web.
  8. #10932 — Voice dictation rejects qwen-audio-3.0-asr-flash as unsupported. Token Plan ASR is unusable because the model-ID allowlist is hardcoded to older IDs.
  9. #17284 — Agent loop: what #17045 leaves to a follow-up. Companion tracking issue ensuring deferred work is not lost at the freeze date.
  10. #17559 — Web Shell mid-turn prompt not recorded in session transcript. The model sees the prompt and replies, but the user message never persists — a transcript-integrity bug.

Also worth watching: a wave of Java SDK bug reports filed 2026-11-17 by @Afloat16 — #17640 (leaked child processes), #17641 (tool-use input discarded), #17642 (file reads joined with path separators), #17656 (lost message UUIDs), #17600/#17627 (transport deadlocks and JSONL corruption), and #17602/#17625 (unscoped cancel, swallowed JSON-RPC errors).

4. Key PR Progress

  1. #17372 — fix(core): retain arguments after shell redirections in permission rules, so git > /dev/null push origin main still yields Bash(git push *) without over-granting subcommands.
  2. #17477 — fix(core): deliver background async hook output to the model, fixing capability-ledger defect L11.
  3. #17530 — fix(core): scope Grep fallback strategies to the git-aware corpus so fallback search matches the git-grep arm exactly.
  4. #17654 — fix(serve): prevent automatic background work from blocking worktree restore (cold worktree recovery path).
  5. #17557 — fix(web-shell): align managed error rendering with DAC and remove the recovery panel above the conversation.
  6. #17421 — feat(web-shell): add a Traditional Chinese (zh-TW/zh-HK/zh-Hant) UI locale with a dedicated Taiwan catalog.
  7. #17676 — fix(web-shell): surface background work on sidebar session rows with an amber busy marker.
  8. #17663 — feat(web-shell): show the SSE admission cap beside stream occupancy in the daemon status dialog.
  9. #11220 — perf(web-shell): gzip serve responses for large transcript loads (long-running perf item from #6181).
  10. #16784 — fix(core): fail closed on undecodable shell paths — security-relevant, denying allow verdicts when filenames can't be losslessly resolved.

Plus active managed-agent work: #17681 (attachment retirement notifications, suspension-wait aging) and #17680 (continuation-ready parks in the epoch-less resubmission arm).

5. Hot Discussions

No Discussions data was provided in this dataset.

6. Feature Request Trends

  • Subscription & provider parity — Make built-in tools (image_gen, Token Plan ASR) honor Qwen subscription/OAuth auth (#17666, #10932).
  • Multi-agent maturity — Capacity/idle-reclamation models (#15082), reliable teammate messaging (#15738), and resilient A2A task handling (#13738).
  • 1.x loop kernel completion — Systematic migration of all surfaces onto the event-driven query() kernel (#17045, #17284, #17237).
  • Web Shell worktree/UI parity — Worktree retention, snapshots, configurable roots, touch-friendly pickers, and locale coverage.

7. Developer Pain Points

  • CI/CD instability is the top frustration — The Managed Agent gate failure (#14724, 431 comments), CVE audit failures (#13078), and flaky tests like #16091 and #17558 repeatedly consume maintainer bandwidth.
  • Java SDK correctness debt — A dense cluster of P2 bugs (process leaks, charset dependence, JSON-RPC error swallowing, corrupted JSONL framing, lost UUIDs) suggests the legacy Java SDK needs a focused hardening pass.
  • Headless/SDK latency and transcript integrity — Non-interactive mode waits on auto-memory tasks (#13851) and Web Shell mid-turn prompts vanish from transcripts (#17559).
  • Multi-agent reliability under ACP/serve — Message delivery, capacity control, and transient-failure recovery remain unresolved for production multi-agent use.
  • Subscription feature gating — Users on paid Qwen plans expect first-party tools (image generation, ASR) to work out of the box.

item.content:encoded:
OpenClaw Ecosystem Digest 2026-11-18

Issues: 472 | PRs: 500 | Projects covered: 5 | Generated: 2026-11-18 02:50 UTC

  • OpenClaw
  • Hermes Agent
  • IronClaw
  • QwenPaw
  • ZeroClaw

OpenClaw Deep Dive

OpenClaw Project Digest — 2026-11-18

1. Today's Overview

OpenClaw remains in a high-velocity but strained maintenance phase. Activity is exceptionally heavy — 472 issues and 500 PRs touched in 24h — yet the open/active ratio (361 open vs. 111 closed issues; 245 open vs. 255 merged/closed PRs) shows the queue is being worked aggressively without net clearing. The single release this cycle, v2026.11.5, is a stability-focused patch addressing restart-safe conversations and safer rollback on failed updates. Underneath the surface, a recurring cluster of state-migration, SQLite/WAL contention, and update-repair deadlock issues continues to dominate the highest-severity (P0/P1) backlog, several of which have been open since September. Community engagement is real but thin per-item (top issues carry 10–42 comments), suggesting a small, technically deep user base filing detailed reproductions rather than broad casual adoption.

2. Releases

v2026.11.5 (latest)

Highlights:

  • Restart-safe conversations — Queued messages, send permissions, and final chat writes are now retained across Gateway restarts (#196923, #196540, #196493). Authored by @steipete.
  • Safer updates — Failed Doctor or Gateway startup now rolls back an attempted activation, reducing the "partially finalized" update class of failures.

Migration / operational notes:

  • No explicit breaking changes documented in the release note excerpt.
  • However, community reports tied to this release cycle indicate that rollback after state migration is still restricted (state-migrated-no-rollback), which remains a source of update deadlock (see #197083, #161921, #183479 below).
  • Users on 2026.11.1–2026.11.3 should note that post-install Doctor WAL publication verification can leave an update "partially finalized" (#197083).

Assessment: This is a corrective release, not a feature release. The rollback-safety work is directionally correct but does not yet resolve the broader class of migration/rollback interdependency bugs.

3. Project Progress

Merged/closed PRs (255 total in 24h). Notable closures and their impact:

  • #191324 [CLOSED] — improve(agents): name the child's runtime and credential on spawn receipts. This advanced spawn-receipt observability, exposing resolvedRuntime, resolvedAuth, and resolvedAuthProfile for primary models. Directly enabled follow-up test work (#200943).
  • #112313 [CLOSED] — Dead-lettered outbound delivery queue entries are permanent. A long-standing (since July) data-retention bug where failed delivery rows could never be read, retried, or cleared. Its closure removes a permanent health counter leak.
  • #158592 [CLOSED] — After host sleep/wake, prepared model runtime publication times out and never recovers. A P0 message-loss bug closed after ~7 weeks.
  • #158070 [CLOSED] — Preflight compaction fails with "agent tool caller authority is no longer active". A P1 message-loss bug affecting multi-agent deployments.
  • #191818, #187468, #137265, #153417, #155396, #138561 — A broad sweep of P1/P2 behavior, auth-provider, and memory bugs closed in this window.

Features advanced (still open but active):

  • #193550 — Plugin hook before_model_request to let plugins gate the final provider request (fail-closed policy hook). XL change, compatibility-flagged, awaiting author.
  • #196203 — Install local projects/templates through a live Gateway (openclaw templates add ./my-template).
  • #198455 — Allow plugins to contribute Prometheus metric families to the existing scrape route.
  • #141004 — Record observed runtime skill usage in the durable audit surface.

Observation: The project is closing older P1s effectively, but the incoming rate of new P1/P0 issues (see §5) roughly offsets it — net backlog is not shrinking.

4. Community Hot Topics

Ranked by comment count. Note that 👍 counts are strikingly low (0–4), indicating discussion is concentrated among a few highly engaged reporters.

Rank Item Comments Link
1 #164294 — Gateway state DB WAL auto-checkpoint never completes (blocked by in-process reader) 42 openclaw/openclaw#164294
2 #191944 — gateway stop / stop --force fail on macOS ("Process ancestry could not be fully inspected") 35 #191944
3 #150635 — Short-term recall retention evicts entries nightly; dreaming deep phase never promotes 29 #150635
4 #178359 — doctor --fix --non-interactive idles 15+ min, never reaches agent DB repair 26 #178359
5 #168955 — Startup regression 2026.10.1: ready ~1030s vs ~410s (Windows) 22 #168955
6 #197083 — Post-install Doctor WAL publication leaves 11.3 update partially finalized 21 #197083
7 #126360 — AgentSelectionRequiredError log flood under explicit multi-agent ownership 21 #126360
8 #48003 — Steer mode does not inject messages mid-turn for main sessions 20 (👍4) #48003

Underlying needs analysis:

  • Operational reliability of the state layer is the dominant theme: WAL checkpointing (#164294), update finalization (#197083), doctor repair hangs (#178359), and startup regressions (#168955) all point to SQLite/state-management fragility as the project's central stability risk.
  • Multi-agent deployments are a first-class use case (#126360, #48003, #155868, #194451) — users are running 6–7 agents with sessions_send routing and hitting coordination edge cases (turn claims, log floods, prompt-cache invalidation).
  • The "dreaming"/memory system is under scrutiny (#150635) — the deep-phase promotion pipeline silently stalls at cap, undermining a headline feature.

5. Bugs & Stability

Ranked by severity (P0 > P1), with fix-PR status noted.

P0 (release blockers)

  • #161921 — After state-migrated-no-rollback, doctor --fix and plugins update each require the other; plugins stuck on previous release. No fix PR. (link)
  • #153426 — Curated memory roots (MEMORY.md/USER.md) silently and permanently excluded from bootstrap injection by the provenance ratchet; needs security review. No fix PR. (link)
  • #89278 — Codex OAuth refresh succeeds but cron/heartbeat fail with 10s auth refresh timeout. Linked PR open. (link)

P1 (crash / message-loss / data-loss)

  • #178359 — doctor --fix --non-interactive hangs 15+ min, never repairs agent DB (macOS). No fix PR. (link)
  • #168955 — Startup regression: sidecars.control-ui-assets blocks 477s on Windows. No fix PR. (link)
  • #185578 — Gateway heap floor only ratchets up; ~25 MiB/h leak until V8 cap aborts. Not repro on main. (link)
  • #181120 — macOS Gateway hangs with main thread blocked closing a worker MessagePort. Related PR #181551 open (disables auto-profiler to avoid native lock stall). (link)
  • #167406 — Windows MSIX: Codex-enabled Gateway startup starves main thread. No fix PR. (link)
  • #194403 — Helper-completion continuations invalidate their own authority; conversations blocked. No fix PR. (link)
  • #194451 — /think (and other directives) mid-turn kill the turn with SqliteTranscriptMutationConflictError; #192585 only covered /status. Linked PR open. (link)
  • #157255 — Turn claim not released after lane timeout; session wedged 90+ min. No fix PR. (link)
  • #196505 — memory index --force aborts with "worker task capacity reached" instead of retrying on large corpora. No fix PR. (link)
  • #117262 — SQLite contention: 3 concurrent write handles cause ~33s event-loop stalls (DEF-61). No fix PR. (link)
  • #152965 — Hot-reloading a non-channel plugin disposes channel plugins without reconnecting; drops inbound messages. No fix PR. (link)
  • #166641 — web_fetch cold fallback synchronously captures unrelated plugins on main thread, causing liveness stalls. Linked PR open. (link)

P2 (notable)

  • #164294 (42 comments) — WAL auto-checkpoint never completes. No fix PR.
  • #197083 — Update partially finalized after WAL publication failure. No fix PR.
  • #182891 — Prompt cache never reused; cache read dropped N -> 0 on every request. No fix PR.
  • #192667 — macOS Settings slowness + dark-theme input visibility — reporter confirms both resolved on 2026.11.5. (link)

Fix-PR coverage note: Of the top-severity items, only a minority (#181120, #89278, #194451, #166641) have linked fix PRs. The most-commented and most-reproduced bugs (WAL checkpoint, doctor hang, state-migration deadlock) remain unfixed with no PR, which is the project's clearest health risk.

6. Feature Requests & Roadmap Signals

Request Issue Likelihood in next release
Mandatory Memory/Embedding setup in onboarding wizard #16670 Medium — low complexity, addresses a known adoption gap; P3 but widely felt
Enforceable checkpoints / bounded yields for long WebChat runs #138990 Medium — needs product decision, tied to foreground-run UX
Context budget / skip policy for Skill Workshop on oversized sessions #150238 Low-Medium — linked PR open, awaiting product decision
Plugin hook to gate final model provider request (before_model_request) PR #193550 Medium — XL PR active, but compatibility-flagged and awaiting author
Install local templates via live Gateway PR #196203 Medium — closes a concrete authoring gap
Plugin-contributed Prometheus metric families PR #198455 Medium — operational observability demand

Prediction: The next minor release is most likely to ship operational/observability improvements (Prometheus plugin metrics, template installation, spawn-receipt naming) rather than the higher-effort product decisions (checkpoint enforcement, memory onboarding). The memory/embedding onboarding step is the most likely user-facing addition because it is low-risk and addresses a documented setup failure.

7. User Feedback Summary

Pain points (ranked by frequency/severity):

  1. Updates break installations. Multiple reporters describe updates that fail at package-swap, leave state "partially finalized," or deadlock repair (#197083, #161921, #183479, #187468, #200756). One Windows user (#200756) hit a baseline package scan failure on beta.2→beta.4. This is the single most damaging theme for user trust.
  2. Startup and runtime performance regressions. #168955 (Windows startup 2.5× slower), #185578 (memory leak), #117262 (33s event-loop stalls) — users are measuring and reporting precisely, indicating production deployments under real load.
  3. Multi-agent coordination failures. Log floods, turn-claim wedges, prompt-cache misses, and duplicate messages (#126360, #48003, #157255, #39476, #155868).
  4. Memory system unreliability. Recall eviction (#150635), indexing failures (#196505), and silent memory-root exclusion (#153426) undercut a headline feature.

Satisfaction signals:

  • Users are highly engaged and technically capable — detailed repros, V8 profiles, symbolized samples. This is a committed, self-hosting audience.
  • #192667's reporter confirming resolution on 2026.11.5 shows fixes do land and are acknowledged.
  • Low 👍 counts suggest a small but deep community rather than a broad one; there is little "casual" feedback noise.

Dissatisfaction signals:

  • Repeated "still reproduces on current main" updates on long-lived issues (e.g., #167609, #141474) indicate maintainer response latency relative to reporter effort.
  • The state-migrated-no-rollback pattern is a recurring source of frustration because it removes the user's escape hatch.

8. Backlog Watch

Long-unanswered or high-impact items needing maintainer attention (all open, no fix PR unless noted):

Issue Age Why it needs attention
#48003 — Steer mode does not inject mid-turn Since 2026-03-16 (~8 mo) P1 session-state/message-loss; highest 👍 (4) on the board; core UX feature
#89278 — Codex OAuth cron/heartbeat 10s timeout Since 2026-06-02 (~5.5 mo) P0; linked PR open but stalled
#117262 — SQLite 3-handle contention (DEF-61) Since 2026-08-01 (~3.5 mo) P1 crash-loop; root-cause of many stall reports
#126360 — AgentSelectionRequiredError log flood Since 2026-08-19 (~3 mo) P2 but 21 comments; explicit multi-agent config
#153426 — Memory roots silently excluded (provenance ratchet) Since 2026-09-20 (~2 mo) P0, needs security review; data-loss for memory feature
#161921 — doctor/plugins mutual dependency after no-rollback Since 2026-09-30 (~7 wk) P0 release blocker; no PR
#164294 — WAL auto-checkpoint never completes Since 2026-10-03 (~6 wk) Most-commented issue (42); no fix PR
#178359 — doctor --fix hangs 15+ min Since 2026-10-20 (~4 wk) P1 crash-loop; blocks recovery from other bugs

  • Deep investment in SQLite/WAL as the durable substrate with an in-process reader model — this is the source of both OpenClaw's durability and its worst bottleneck (auto-checkpoint never completes, 3-handle contention causing 33s event-loop stalls).

Activity tiers:

  • Tier 1 — High-velocity, strained: OpenClaw (~1,000 events/24h). Iterating fastest, but intake ≈ closure → net backlog flat. Rapidly iterating, not stabilizing.
  • Tier 2 — High-velocity, healthier: QwenPaw (~73 events, 12 issues closed, 21 PRs merged). Rapidly iterating with real churn — the most balanced project. ZeroClaw (~71 events, 9 PRs closed) is close but closure-starved on S1s.
  • Tier 3 — Moderate velocity, stalling: Hermes Agent (~100 events, 0 issues closed). Iterating in PR count but not converging. Risk of reporter fatigue.
  • Tier 4 — Low/automated: IronClaw (10 Dependabot PRs, 0 human activity). Maintainer-review-lag phase.

Maturity signals:

  • Most mature safety posture: ZeroClaw (S0/S1 triage discipline, RUSTSEC tracking, sandbox RFC).
  • Most mature release-velocity on features: QwenPaw (same-day fix PRs, plugin marketplace shipping).
  • Least mature continuity: Hermes (canary release with no changelog; critical security issue #59293 open 4.5 months with needs-decision).

Contributor health: QwenPaw and ZeroClaw both received same-day fixes from first-time or external contributors (#8701, #11598) — a healthy signal. OpenClaw's author concentration (e.g., @steipete on the release) suggests bus-factor risk. IronClaw shows zero contributor signal.

7. Trend Signals

For AI agent developers and platform decision-makers:

  1. The state layer is the product. SQLite/WAL contention (OpenClaw #117262, #164294), session FIFOs (Hermes #157169), cron locks (ZeroClaw #9191), and admission conflicts (Hermes #150056) all point to the same conclusion: durable session state with self-healing reconciliation is now the differentiator, not model choice or tool count. Buyers should evaluate agent frameworks on their failure modes after restart, mid-turn interruption, and profile switch — not on demo polish.

  2. Security controls are failing open by default. Three independent projects report approval/emergency/hook controls that silently do nothing in production deployments (Hermes #100942 under systemd, ZeroClaw #9390 runtime emergency stop, OpenClaw #153426 memory provenance). Fail-closed must be the default; audit each entry point. Expect enterprise RFPs to demand this within 2–3 release cycles.

  3. Plugin extensibility is the new moat — and the new attack surface. Four of five projects are extracting subsystems into plugins. The downstream need is a stable semantic contract: theming tokens (QwenPaw #8071), pre-request hooks (OpenClaw #193550), OAuth for remote MCP (ZeroClaw #12449). New plugins must be able to gate — not just decorate — the request path.

  4. Channel breadth is a QA liability. QwenPaw's WeChat ACCOUNT_IN_USE duplicate reports (#8709, #8693) and DingTalk session collision (#8771) show that shipping many channels without per-adapter isolation invariants creates silent cross-user data mixing. Channel plugins need conformance tests before release.

  5. Configuration semantics must be honest. ZeroClaw's cost.enforcement.mode: "warn" that still stops turns (#12477), QwenPaw's quota-error misclassification (#8776), and OpenClaw's context-budget gaps (#150238) all erode operator trust. A config flag that doesn't do what it says is worse than no flag.

  6. The memory feature is a trust surface, not a novelty. OpenClaw's stalling deep-phase promotion (#150635), silent memory-root exclusion (#153426), and QwenPaw's ReMeLight cost concerns (#7719) reveal that "autonomous memory" is not production-ready in any project today. Treat memory pipelines as security-sensitive data paths, not UX flourishes.

  7. Observability is becoming table-stakes for ops. Prometheus plugin metrics (OpenClaw), per-tool latency reporting (Hermes #11116), and log-level control (ZeroClaw #12476) are being requested by self-hosting operators — signaling that agents are entering the "boring infrastructure" phase where SRE tooling matters more than capability headlines.

Bottom line for developers choosing a framework: QwenPaw currently offers the best forward-momentum/closure ratio; OpenClaw offers the richest capability surface at the cost of state-layer debt; ZeroClaw is the best fit for security-sensitive deployments; Hermes Agent needs to demonstrate issue-closure velocity before it can be recommended for production; IronClaw is not a candidate for external adoption at this time.

QwenPaw — agentscope-ai/QwenPaw

QwenPaw Project Digest — 2026-11-18

1. Today's Overview

QwenPaw shows very high activity in the last 24 hours: 23 issues updated (11 open, 12 closed) and 50 PRs touched (29 open, 21 merged/closed), with no new releases. The project is in a post-2.3.0 stabilization phase, with a heavy cluster of bug reports around the new WeChat/DingTalk channel plugins, the Creator plugin, and console UI regressions. Notably, the DoomLoopGate bug (#8700) received a fix PR (#8701) the same day it was discussed, indicating responsive maintainer triage. At the same time, long-running feature work continues on plugin architecture (#8554, #8469, #8499) and mobile (#7378, #8796), suggesting the roadmap is pivoting toward a plugin-extensible, multi-platform assistant. Overall project health is good but strained: volume of duplicate channel bugs (WeChat ACCOUNT_IN_USE reported twice: #8709, #8693) suggests release QA gaps for channel integrations.

2. Releases

No new releases in the last 24 hours. Latest referenced stable is v2.3.0.post1; users on 2.2.x and 2.3.0 are reporting channel and console issues that appear addressed on main.

3. Project Progress

Merged/closed PRs today (21 total) include several long-lived fixes finally landing:

  • #2367 [CLOSED] fix(console): harden session deletion flow — adds timestamped chats.json.backup-* snapshots before destructive deletes and aligns batch delete payloads. Directly relevant to the session-loss complaints in #7724. Link
  • #2355 [CLOSED] fix(console): add space between bot prefix and message text — fixes Telegram output Georgehello how are you → George hello how are you. Link
  • #2142 [CLOSED] fix: add BiDi text support for RTL languages — CSS direction: auto / unicode-bidi: plaintext for chat input and message areas. Link
  • #8151 [CLOSED] fix(local_models): parse llama.cpp build numbers without false updates — fixes false "update available" prompts. Link
  • #8166 [CLOSED] docs(heartbeat): document runtime semantics — adds runtime behavior docs for heartbeat (silence, concurrency, reloads). Link
  • #8795 [CLOSED] fix(channels): lower minimum QwenPaw version to 2.3.0.post1 — unblocks channel plugin installation on the latest patch release. Link
  • #7378 [CLOSED] [DO NOT MERGE] feat(mobile): QwenPaw native mobile experience — Expo/React Native client closed without merge; mobile direction now appears to route through #8793 (Platform Web App). Link

Open PRs advancing major features: #8554 (plugin CLI + extension points, size/XXXL), #8469 (extract MCP into a plugin), #8499 (extract local model management into a plugin), #8793 (Platform Web App access), and #7719 (separate model for ReMeLight memory writing).

4. Community Hot Topics

  • #8071 [OPEN] Plugin-facing theme extension point — 18 comments, the most-discussed issue. Plugin authors are limited to a single colorPrimary knob while the console theme system supports 6 palettes plus accent/hover/background/surface/radius. Underlying need: a stable, semantic plugin theming contract so third-party plugins can match console UX without forking CSS. Link
  • #7724 [CLOSED] 会话丢失 (Session loss) — 6 comments. A Windows 2.2.1 desktop user lost an entire conversation (and their model config) after a plugin redeploy/shutdown mid-task. The session never reappeared in the console. High user-trust impact; the closed #2367 session-deletion hardening is likely related. Link
  • #8595 [CLOSED] Plugin install fails with 'No package metadata was found' for qwenpaw-creator — 5 comments. Both UI and CLI hot-install paths failed for official plugin v2.0.4. Fixed in the 2.3.0.post1 timeframe. Link
  • #7745 [CLOSED] Agent switch deletes last session & makes history unclickable — 4 comments. Two concrete console bookkeeping defects on every agent switch; user notes landing on a blank chat is intentional per #7687 but the data loss is not. Link
  • #8521 [CLOSED] Missing replies + Ctrl+C requires multiple presses — 4 comments. Two distinct complaints: intermittent empty answers, and clipboard copy failing on first press in Chrome and Edge; user also requests a legacy UI toggle. Link
  • #8774 [OPEN] Mid-turn steer (send-now) for running chats — contributor with a working local implementation seeking design feedback. Signals strong demand for interruptible, steerable agents across all channels. Link

5. Bugs & Stability

Ranked by severity (most severe first):

  1. #7724 [CLOSED] Session + model config loss (desktop, Win10, 2.2.1) — data loss of an entire conversation after plugin redeploy/shutdown. Mitigation appears to be the session-deletion hardening in #2367. Link
  2. #8709 / #8693 [CLOSED] WeChat channel ACCOUNT_IN_USE + PLATFORM_RESULT_UNKNOWN (2.3.0) — channel startup path and workspace projection both reserve the same runtime key; successful sends misreported. Two independent reports of the same root cause → release QA gap. Link · Link
  3. #8700 [OPEN] DoomLoopGate never triggers (2.3.0, Docker + main) — agentscope 2.0.10 appends iterations to one assistant message, so the per-iteration cursor records only the first snapshot; runaway loops go undetected. Fix PR exists: #8701 (first-time contributor). Issue · PR
  4. #8771 [OPEN] DingTalk 1:1 session collision — short_session_id_from_conversation_id() takes the last 8 chars, which are org/robot-constant for 1:1 chats, so all 1:1 chats in one org map to the same session. Cross-user data mixing risk. Link
  5. #8778 / #8779 [OPEN] Creator: expired DashScope signed URL reused; FAILED asset_ingest is terminal — reference-image generation breaks ~24h after artifact creation, and failed ingests 404 forever with no retry path (store already sanctions FAILED→QUEUED). Both reported by same power user on 2.0.6. Link · Link
  6. #8776 [OPEN] classify_model_error misclassifies 400+quota as bad_request — blocks FallbackChatModel from switching when the primary model's quota is exhausted (e.g., dots provider). Link
  7. #8789 [OPEN] Invalid batch task values dispatch sibling subagents before failing — _spawn_batch() validates with .strip() but dispatches the raw value; null/numbers/lists/objects pass preflight, and valid siblings launch before the batch fails. Link
  8. #8796 [OPEN] Mobile full-screen containers render under the system status bar — top safe-area-inset missing since c54a4465 introduced viewport-fit=cover; #4738 fixed only the bottom. Link
  9. #8521 [CLOSED] Intermittent empty replies + Ctrl+C multi-press (2.2.2.post1) — user can't tell if model or app; clipboard issue reproduced in Chrome and Edge. Link
  10. #8798 [CLOSED] MODEL_QUOTA_EXCEEDED on kilo-auto/free — free-tier model quota exhaustion surfaced as a crash-style error dump; related to the fallback gap in #8776. Link

6. Feature Requests & Roadmap Signals

  • Plugin extension surface is the dominant theme: semantic theme tokens (#8071), plugin CLI commands (#8554), MCP-as-plugin (#8469), local-model-as-plugin (#8499). Expect plugin architecture consolidation in 2.3.x/2.4.
  • Mid-turn steer / send-now (#8774) — contributor has a working implementation and wants design feedback; a natural candidate for a 2.4 milestone given multi-channel interest (console, Feishu, WeCom, QQ, DingTalk).
  • save_draft tool for qwenpawmail-mcp (#8780) — agent workflows need write-without-send semantics; low-risk, likely to land soon.
  • Legacy UI toggle (#8521) — repeated user request for a switch between old/new console layouts, plus smoother model switching.
  • Platform Web App access (#8793) — phone QR sign-in to a connected local runtime; supersedes the closed native mobile PR (#7378) and is the clearest next-version signal.
  • Separate memory-writing model (#7719) — cost optimization for ReMeLight (auto_memory/auto_dream/daily_paper/auto_fin).

7. User Feedback Summary

Pain points:

  • Trust in data persistence is eroding — multiple users report losing sessions and model config (#7724, #7745). The closed #2367 backup-before-delete work directly addresses this.
  • Channel reliability on 2.3.0 — WeChat (ACCOUNT_IN_USE) and DingTalk (session collision) are the loudest new complaints; enterprise users are hitting org-wide session merging.
  • Console UX regression — #8521 explicitly says the new UI is "less efficient, less smooth" and asks for a legacy toggle; large idle areas make model switching cumbersome.
  • Intermittent empty replies — undermines confidence, with users unsure whether to blame the model or the app.
  • Free-tier quota handling — #8798's frustrated tone ("i keep getting a damn...") reflects poor error ergonomics for quota exhaustion; #8776 shows the fallback logic won't save them.

Positive signals:

  • Contributors are shipping fixes fast (#8701 same-day for #8700; #8728 declared thinking-off control).
  • Plugin ecosystem is genuinely active — #8071's 18 comments show engaged third-party plugin authors.
  • Users file detailed, well-structured bug reports (e.g., #8716, #8778, #8779 with environment tables and root-cause hypotheses), indicating a sophisticated user base worth investing in.

8. Backlog Watch

Items needing maintainer attention (oldest/highest-impact first):

  • #6952 [OPEN] perf: prefix cache instability from unsorted tool schemas — open since 2026-08-12 (3+ months), only 2 comments. Non-deterministic prompt construction causes unnecessary KV-cache misses on every turn — a direct cost/latency issue for all users. No linked PR. Link
  • #7767 [CLOSED] Guardrail-plugin bug bundle — stale console attachment blob, one-shot cron misfire drop, console tail-drop, on_acting never fires. Closed but with only 3 comments; unclear whether all four sub-bugs were individually fixed. Link
  • #7719 [OPEN] Separate model for ReMeLight memory writing — open since 2026-09-12, size/XL, no merge yet. Blocks cost-sensitive deployments. Link
  • #8469 [OPEN] refactor(mcp): extract mcp into plugin and #8499 [OPEN] extract local model management into plugin — both size/XXXL, open since late October; large refactors that gate the plugin roadmap. Link · Link
  • #8268 [OPEN] fix(task_tracker): bound run completion callback and always clean up — fixes the run-cleanup half of #8173; hung callbacks leave runs running forever. Open since 2026-10-16. Link
  • #8133 [OPEN] fix(console): repair CJK emphasis boundaries in chat Markdown — size/XL, open since 2026-10-08; raw ** markers visible in Chinese text, an ongoing quality issue for the CJK user base. Link
  • #8771 [OPEN] DingTalk session collision — security-adjacent (cross-user session mixing) and has no linked fix PR; should be prioritized above cosmetic issues. Link

Data source: github.com/agentscope-ai/QwenPaw — digest generated for 2026-11-18. Comment counts reflect data provided; PR comment fields were undefined in the source and are omitted.

ZeroClaw — zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw

ZeroClaw Project Digest — 2026-11-18

1. Today's Overview

ZeroClaw remains in a high-activity, pre-release stabilization phase: 21 issues were touched in the last 24h (all still open/active) and 50 PRs were updated, with 9 merged/closed and 41 still open. No new releases were published, but the volume of release:v0.9.1-tagged work (Lucid backend retirement, dependency security fixes, Windows test triage) indicates the v0.9.1 milestone is actively being assembled. The day's activity skews heavily toward bug triage and security hardening — multiple S0/S1 issues were touched, including an emergency-stop enforcement gap and a supervised-SOP approval bypass — suggesting the project is prioritizing correctness and safety over new features right now. Overall health is strong on throughput but strained on stability: several long-lived, high-risk issues remain open with no fix PRs yet.

2. Releases

None. No new releases were published in the last 24h. (Note: several PRs and issues are tagged release:v0.9.1, indicating v0.9.1 is in preparation but not yet cut.)

3. Project Progress

Merged/closed PRs today (9 total; notable items):

  • #9740 [CLOSED] — feat(channels): add VoiceHost WebSocket bridge. A large opt-in bridge allowing external FunASR/SenseVoice audio hosts to exchange transcripts, replies, interruption, and approval events with ZeroClaw. This is a significant voice-channel capability landing after months in the parking lot.
  • #9229 [CLOSED] — fix(runtime): make interactive Ctrl+C state-aware. Reworks the REPL's signal handling into a single persistent Idle/Active/Stopping lifecycle, replacing per-turn listeners. A long-running (July) fix that improves interactive reliability.
  • #11238 [CLOSED] — fix(config): accept tagged declarative cron schedules. Fixes #11237; config PATCH/PUT and /config/cron now correctly save tagged cron schedule objects.
  • #11647 [CLOSED] — fix(providers): decouple vision support from system merge. Corrects a gating bug where image-part support was incorrectly tied to system-prompt merging.
  • #11598 [CLOSED] — feat(security): support glob matching in the command allowlist. Lets operators allow directory trees (e.g., skill/plugin script folders) instead of enumerating every file.
  • #11779 / #11780 [CLOSED] — SOP tooling fixes: sop list now surfaces malformed SOP.toml failures and exits non-zero; max_concurrent_total is documented and named in capacity refusals.

In-flight notable PRs (open): #12521 (retire Lucid memory backend), #12449 (generic OAuth 2.1 + PKCE for remote MCP servers), #11744 (stream reasoning in Telegram/Slack drafts), #12516 (dependency security fixes).

4. Community Hot Topics

  • #8600 — Per-chat model switching for multi-model providers (5 comments, 1 👍, open since July). A moltis migrant requests easy switching between any model a provider supports. Underlying need: users want provider-level model catalogs (e.g., OpenRouter's full set) exposed per conversation without reconfiguring the agent. Tagged status:parking-lot and risk:high — a design-heavy request.

  • #12401 — Tool-context collapse breaks Claude Opus 5.5 chats (5 comments, S1). Once an older tool-using turn leaves the keep_tool_context_turns window, every subsequent request fails with a thinking-signature 400. Underlying need: correct interaction between context-window pruning and Anthropic's signed-thinking contract.

  • #9191 — Cron agent jobs have no wall-clock timeout (5 comments, P1, S1). In-flight locks are only cleared at process start; a hung agent job can block indefinitely. Underlying need: production-grade scheduler isolation and cancellation budgets.

  • #9644 — Retire the Lucid memory backend (4 comments, updated today). Lucid wraps SQLite but shells out to an external lucid command on every store/recall. The corresponding PR #12521 is now open, making this a likely v0.9.1 deliverable.

  • #9390 / #9802 — Emergency stop is CLI-only; RFC for full enforcement (4 and 3 comments, P1, risk:high). A security audit found the emergency-stop state file is never read by runtime paths. The RFC proposes interrupting in-flight tool work and enforcing network-kill/domain-block at the shared egress boundary. This is the most consequential safety gap in the tracker.

5. Bugs & Stability

Ranked by severity:

  • S0 — #12514: Supervised SOP skips approval when step 1's decide question is answered "no." The engine skips step 1 before its approval gate, so a supervised SOP asks for no approval at all. Data-loss/security risk. No fix PR referenced yet.
  • S1 — #12401: Claude Opus 5.5 thinking-signature 400 after tool-context collapse. Workflow-blocking regression since v0.9.0. A related fix exists for a different symptom: PR #12509 stops replaying unsigned thinking blocks (fixes #12504), but the collapse-window interaction itself appears unfixed.
  • S1 — #9191: Cron agent jobs lack wall-clock timeout. No fix PR.
  • S1 — #12477: cost.enforcement.mode is ignored. An exceeded budget always stops the turn even in the default "warn" mode. No fix PR.
  • S1 — #9390: Emergency stop not enforced at runtime. RFC #9802 tracks the fix; a first enforcement slice landed via PR #9440 (per issue text), but full coverage is pending.
  • S2 — #12504: Anthropic provider replays unsigned thinking blocks. Fix PR #12509 is open.
  • S2 — #12492: Dashboard chats ignore runtime-profile thinking settings. No native thinking config is ever sent from the web dashboard. No fix PR.
  • S2 — #12476: Gateway logs every connection at INFO, flooding runtime traces. No fix PR.
  • S2 — #12489: Cron scheduler waits for the whole due batch, so one long agent job delays all others. No fix PR.
  • S3 — #12507: Web chat shows [CURRENT DATE & TIME: …] prefix and synthetic timestamps after reload. Fix PR #12515 is open.

Also of note: #12505 tracks replacement of unmaintained chrono/chrono-tz (RUSTSEC-2026-0543/0555), which currently fails the Security CI job on every build; PR #12516 updates zip for RUSTSEC-2026-0548 and accepts the chrono advisories as a stopgap.

6. Feature Requests & Roadmap Signals

  • Per-chat model switching (#8600) — high user interest, but parked and high-risk; unlikely before v0.9.1.
  • Runtime-profile thinking levels for OpenAI (#12054) and the dashboard counterpart (#12492) — consistent thinking-level plumbing across providers and surfaces. A natural v0.9.1/v0.10 candidate given the adjacent Anthropic thinking fixes already in flight.
  • Scoped operator-managed service credentials (#12422) — an RFC for authorizing agents against services without exposing the underlying credential to the model or chat. Security-model change; likely to mature over multiple releases.
  • Complete emergency-stop enforcement (#9802) — an RFC with a partial implementation already merged; expect incremental slices in v0.9.1+.
  • Lucid memory backend retirement (#9644) — PR #12521 is open and tagged release:v0.9.1; strong candidate for the next release (breaking: configs selecting Lucid migrate to SQLite).
  • Generic MCP OAuth 2.1 + PKCE (#12449) — large XL PR enabling authenticated remote MCP servers; a notable capability expansion if it lands.

Prediction: v0.9.1 will most likely bundle the Lucid retirement, the zip security bump, the SOP/dashboard fixes already in PR, and possibly the Anthropic unsigned-thinking fix. Larger items (OAuth MCP, voice bridge follow-ups, thinking-level parity) look like v0.10 material.

7. User Feedback Summary

Real users are hitting provider-integration friction more than anything else: the Anthropic thinking-signature class of bugs (#12401, #12504) blocks Claude Opus 5.5 users after a few tool turns, and dashboard users report their configured thinking settings are silently ignored (#12492). A moltis migrant (#8600) explicitly praises ZeroClaw's capability parity but flags per-chat model switching as the one missing convenience — a satisfaction signal with a clear gap. Production operators are voicing scheduler and cost-control reliability concerns: cron jobs with no timeout (#9191), batch-serialized cron execution (#12489), and a cost-enforcement mode that doesn't actually warn (#12477). Security-minded users and auditors are driving the emergency-stop thread (#9390/#9802) and the supervised-SOP approval bypass (#12514) — the latter is the most alarming report of the day. Minor but recurring UX papercuts appear in the web dashboard (#12507). Overall sentiment: the feature set is valued, but users are asking for predictable failure modes and honest configuration semantics before adding more surface area.

8. Backlog Watch

Long-unanswered or under-attended items that deserve maintainer attention:

  • #8600 (open since 2026-07-01, parking-lot) — per-chat model switching; four months old with only 5 comments and one 👍. Needs a design decision or explicit deferral.
  • #9191 (open since 2026-07-20, P1/S1) — cron job timeout; nearly four months without a fix PR despite workflow-blocking severity.
  • #9390 (open since 2026-07-26) and #9802 (open since 2026-08-07) — emergency-stop enforcement; partial progress via #9440 but the RFC remains open and high-risk.
  • #9644 (open since 2026-08-01) — Lucid retirement; now has an open PR (#12521), so it is moving, but the issue itself has sat for 3.5 months.
  • #7821 (open since 2026-06-17, XL, risk:high) — canonical sandbox_policy schema with application-layer enforcement; five months open and a foundational security change that likely needs reviewer bandwidth.
  • #12449 (XL, MCP OAuth) — recently active but very large; at risk of review fatigue.

Health note: Throughput is healthy (9 PRs closed, active triage), but the concentration of S0/S1 issues without fix PRs (#12514, #9191, #12477, #12489) and the five-month-old security PR #7821 are the main risks to the v0.9.1 timeline. The Lucid retirement and dependency-security work are the clearest, best-scoped wins to close first.

item.content:encoded:
AI Infrastructure Digest 2026-11-18

Generated: 2026-11-18 02:50 UTC | Projects covered: 6

  • vLLM
  • SGLang
  • llama.cpp
  • Ollama
  • LiteLLM
  • Unsloth

Cross-Project Comparison

Cross-Project Comparison Report — AI Infrastructure Digest

Date: 2026-11-18 | Scope: vLLM, SGLang, llama.cpp, Ollama, LiteLLM, Unsloth

1. Ecosystem Overview

The 2026-11-18 digest confirms a market that has bifurcated into production serving engines (vLLM, SGLang) racing on frontier hardware (Blackwell SM120, MI355X/gfx950, Ascend NPU) and local/edge runtimes (llama.cpp, Ollama) quietly absorbing multimodal and TTS workloads. The dominant engineering theme across the top two engines is no longer raw throughput but silent correctness: vLLM disclosed a SwiGLU clamp omission producing severe log-prob mismatches, and SGLang reported fp16 MHA NaN that degrades output without a crash. Meanwhile LiteLLM is executing the most architecturally significant change of the day — a native Rust rewrite of the proxy data plane — while simultaneously fixing long-standing O(n²) and memory-retention bugs in the Python path. On the training side, Unsloth's silent drop of MoE router aux loss (corrected only today) reinforces that eval-equivalence across framework versions remains an unsolved trust problem. The layer that benefits most from today's work is agent/tool-calling, where reliability is now the binding constraint rather than model capability.

2. Activity Comparison

Project Layer Issues (open / notable) PRs (open / notable) Release status (last 24h) Breaking-change signal
vLLM Serving engine (datacenter) ~10 ranked stability items; trackers with 36+ comments ~15 active perf/feature PRs, 6-PR ROCm stack None RFC: weight reload semantics (Rev 2); frontend tool_choice divergence
SGLang Serving engine (datacenter) CUDA coredump tracker (380); CI flakiness (211); 33–45% regression KDA overflow, grammar LRU, SPF reservation, HiCache None 1.0 tracker converts silent config → errors
llama.cpp Local runtime (library/server) ~16 ranked; Vulkan/RDNA3, i915, SYCL Kokoro TTS, conv2d F32, few-row MMQ, V100 MoE b12484–b12494 merged grammar+ignore_eos now returns HTTP 400
Ollama Local runtime (product) ~9 ranked; RDNA1 regression, glm-ocr EOS CANN/Ascend, MLX cache, VRAM splitting, streaming buffer None None
LiteLLM Gateway / proxy ~10 ranked; read-replica dead, audit 500, stream builder Rust gateway port (multiple), FIPS AES-GCM, cache-key fix v1.110.0, v1.111.0-rc.1, v1.108.11 LTS enable_projects_ui removed; FIPS crypto swap
Unsloth Fine-tuning / Studio ~10 ranked; ROCm VAE NaN, qk_norm bug, privacy log MCP OAuth, alias configs, MoE aux-loss fix, log redaction v0.1.919-beta SFT loss baseline moves on TRL ≥ 1.18

Reading the table: vLLM and SGLang show the highest engineering throughput on frontier kernels; llama.cpp is the only project with same-day merged commits at volume; LiteLLM is the only project shipping a release + RC + LTS in one window, and the only one undergoing a language-level rewrite.

3. Model Support Race

New model landings in this window:

Model vLLM SGLang llama.cpp Ollama Unsloth
DeepSeek-V4-Flash / V4.1 (incl. Vision) ✅ RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell preset (8/4-GPU) ✅ FP8 DeepGEMM Hopper + gfx950/RDNA trackers — — —
Kimi K3 ✅ structured-output protocol (draft) ✅ MLA under DCP (NPU) — — —
Qwen3.5 / 3.8 family tracker issues (3.5-27B slow batch) ✅ MTP quant fix on NPU — tool-call parser bug ✅ 27B GGUF + llama-server
GLM DSA / GLM-5.3-Flash — ✅ Ascend layer-split; SM120 fa4 crash — — —
Gemma 4 26B MLX — — — — ✅ vision bug fixed
MiniMax-H3-Image — — — — ✅ GGUF/FP8/INT8 + LoRA (first)
Kokoro TTS / Qwen3-TTS ICL — — ✅ merged (b12494/b12491) — —
gpt-oss 500-error fix PR open — — — ✅ aux-loss SFT fix
PPLX Decider v1.3 — — — ✅ MLX 27B + Flash —

Verdict:

  • vLLM is ahead on frontier datacenter architectures (DeepSeek-V4-Flash-Vision on sm_120 with validated placement presets is a shipping-grade artifact, not a feature request).
  • SGLang is ahead on Chinese-model + NPU breadth — it is the only engine with credible Ascend coverage across GLM DSA, Kimi K3, and Qwen3.5 MTP.
  • llama.cpp now leads on audio — Kokoro and Qwen3-TTS merging into mtmd makes it the only project where text, vision, and speech share one pipeline.
  • Unsloth is the only project shipping quantized multimodal training for a new model on day one (MiniMax-H3-Image).

4. Performance Frontier

Optimization effort today clusters unevenly:

  • vLLM — ROCm/gfx950 decode-step launch fusion. Six stacked PRs collapse sparse-MLA top-k from 4 launches to 1, eliminate 4 launches per decode step in compression, and reduce 8-block+merge to a single block for few-row top-512. This is kernel-launch-count optimization — the most mature form of inference tuning and a strong signal that AMD MI355X is now a first-class target. Secondary: last-layer FFN pruning during prefill (broadly applicable, mathematically equivalence-preserving).

  • SGLang — KV cache & scheduler economics. HiCache unified-memory page-envelope work (hole compaction, row-granular copies) and SPF dual-budget reservation address memory-hierarchy throughput under multi-turn load. The EAGLE fused draft-softmax+sample kernel targets speculative-decoding latency. Notably, SGLang is fighting a 33–45% SM90 decode regression — optimization here is partly defensive.

  • llama.cpp — CUDA kernel dispatch correctness. Few-row MMQ for MoE decode (DGX Spark), conv2d F32 implicit GEMM, V100 MMQ routing (fixing a silent slow path where FP16 tensor cores exist but INT8 tensor cores don't), and native quantized KV dequant in flash attention. The discipline is notable: quantized matvec fusion was proactively disabled on Pascal rather than shipped with a regression.

  • Ollama — infrastructure & allocation efficiency. 8 MB per-call streaming buffer → on-demand; VRAM accounting fixes ending unnecessary model splits/evictions; context-shift no longer forces reloads.

  • LiteLLM — gateway hot-path de-quadraticization. Cache-key construction no longer stringifies the full request (200 MB payloads were spending seconds on the event loop); credential sync went from O(n²) with 10s+ blocking reloads to Rust/SQLx; router now uses per-deployment tokenizers instead of gpt-3.5's (9–14% context over-count).

Cross-cutting observation: the frontier has shifted from "make a token faster" to (a) eliminate redundant kernel launches, (b) remove silent correctness gaps in fast paths, (c) fix algorithmic complexity in control planes.

5. Layer Positioning

┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│  FINE-TUNING / TRAINING       │  Unsloth (Studio + kernels)     │
├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│  GATEWAY / PROXY              │  LiteLLM (Python → Rust port)   │
├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│  SERVING ENGINES (datacenter)  │  vLLM      │  SGLang            │
│  → multi-GPU, PD-disagg, MoE,  │  (broad    │  (NPU/China-model  │
│    spec decoding, KV tiers     │   coverage)│   + unified memory)│
├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│  LOCAL RUNTIMES                │  llama.cpp  │  Ollama            │
│  → GGUF, single-node, mtmd,    │  (library)  │  (product/UX)      │
│    TTS, edge GPUs              │             │                    │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

  • Serving engines (vLLM, SGLang) compete on scale-out correctness and hardware coverage. vLLM's differentiator is breadth (ROCm, Intel XPU FP8, Blackwell sm_120, Rust frontend). SGLang's is depth on NPU + Chinese frontier models, plus PD-disaggregation with unified memory. Both are converging on silent-config → explicit-error policies (SGLang 1.0 tracker; vLLM's frontend divergence RFC).

  • Local runtimes (llama.cpp, Ollama) occupy different sub-layers: llama.cpp is the engine/library (mtmd now unifies text, vision, TTS); Ollama is the productization layer (VRAM splitting, model loading, streaming, CANN backend). Ollama's roadmap increasingly looks like "llama.cpp + UX + hardware abstraction."

  • Gateway (LiteLLM) is the only project in the set executing a full control-plane language migration (Python → Rust gateway via router-core). This is the clearest signal that gateway latency, not model latency, is becoming the SLO bottleneck in multi-provider deployments.

  • Training/fine-tuning (Unsloth) sits orthogonally, but its TRL ≥ 1.18 aux-loss correction and MCP search-only listing both directly affect inference-time behavior (checkpoint comparability; prompt-cache stability).

6. Trend Signals

Six trends extracted from today's activity:

  1. Silent correctness is the headline risk of 2026.

    • vLLM: DeepGEMM SwiGLU clamp omission → 9 severe token mismatches per 16K tokens (#68084).
    • SGLang: fp16 MHA decode NaN when a single q·k exceeds 65504 (#51095).
    • Unsloth: MoE router aux loss silently dropped on TRL ≥ 1.18 (#18230).
    • llama.cpp: pattern silently overriding minLength/maxLength (#30749).
    • Watch: stop treating "it runs" as "it's correct"; add log-prob-diff and NaN canaries to CI across at least two engines.

  2. The Rust control plane is the new competitive battleground.

    • LiteLLM porting the proxy to a native Rust gateway (router-core, SQLx auth, Rust middleware).
    • vLLM exposing a Rust HTTP frontend (with a known tool_choice semantic divergence vs Python, #66858).
    • SGLang's Rust frontend at multimodal parity deficit (Qwen-VL only, #48705).
    • Watch: gateway frontends are fragmenting by language; pin your adapter semantics and test tool-calling explicitly.

  3. Tool-call and streaming fidelity is the agent stack's weakest link.

    • vLLM (gpt-oss 500 on special tokens in prior tool names), LiteLLM (parallel tool-call args dropped in Codex streaming #45348), Ollama (Qwen XML parse failures #14834), llama.cpp (bare-JSON Llama 3.x skips lazy grammar #32496), SGLang (Anthropic streaming drops closing }, #42260).
    • Watch: validate tool-call JSON at your application boundary; do not trust streamed delimiters from any engine today.

  4. KV cache is migrating from "a tensor" to "a tiered memory system."

    • SGLang HiCache unified-memory page-envelope work; vLLM KV-offload promotion lifecycle redesign (#66782) and the 1.0–1.8s re-queue stall (#62532); llama.cpp native quantized KV in flash attention (#31234).
    • Watch: tiered KV (HBM → host → NVMe/RDMA) is becoming a first-class configurable resource; budget for promotion-latency SLOs, not just hit rates.

  5. Frontier hardware has pluralized — AMD and Ascend are no longer experimental.

    • vLLM: 6-PR gfx950/MI355X stack, Intel XPU FP8 unification (Xe3p prefers W8A8).
    • SGLang: ROCm trackers (DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, Qwen3.8-27B MXFP4) + AMD correctness fixes (RCCL routing for gfx1250, ROCm 7.2 masked SDPA).
    • Ollama: CANN/Ascend NPU build + device discovery PR (#19732).
    • Watch: if you evaluate only NVIDIA, you are now leaving validated capacity on the table.

  6. Multimodal + audio is consolidating into single-process inference.

    • llama.cpp: Kokoro TTS + Qwen3-TTS ICL merged into mtmd (speech synthesis in the same server).
    • Unsloth: Computer Use (beta) with MCP integrations for Unity/Unreal/Blender/Roblox.
    • vLLM: Rust frontend multimodal metadata (mm_payload: "metadata") for encoder-cache transfer.
    • Watch: voice and screen-driving agents can now collapse multiple services into one process — simplify your deployment topology.

The revision reverses the Rev 1 approach of skipping post-load processing on reload, after validating across 17 flagship model families. Rev 1 caused silent correctness errors (stale MLA absorbed weights; loaders bypassing post-load). If you build RL training loops that reload weights into a running engine, treat any pre-Rev-2 behavior as unsafe and re-read the updated contract.

4. Performance & Optimization

ROCm / gfx950 (MI355X) — DeepSeek-V4.1, stacked series:

  • PR #67365 — decode sparse-MLA ragged top-k built in 1 launch instead of 4, from MXFP4 indexer row bounds (DEP8 path).
  • PR #67367 — few-row gfx950 top-512 calls (≤32 rows, 16K–36K positions) stay in one block instead of 8 blocks + merge.
  • PR #67366 — folds consumer remap into top-512 and skips the −1 fill on all decode rows.
  • PR #67364 — compression launch writes cache records itself: 4 fewer launches per decode step (4 kv-source layers).
  • PR #67584 — AITER MegaMoE picks small/large/staged route per call from DP-group max rows instead of always staged.

Other:

Ranked by severity:

  1. Batched DeepGEMM missing SwiGLU clamp → silent correctness mismatch — PR #68084. DeepSeek-V4-Flash-Base sets swiglu_limit=10; with deepep_low_latency on 8×H200, batched DeepGEMM omitted the clamp, producing 9 severe token log-probability mismatches in 16,384 tokens (one token at −0.31 vs −31.68). Fix PR open. This is a correctness bug, not just a perf issue.
  2. gpt-oss chat completions 500 on special-token text in prior tool-call names — Issue #65770 / PR #65771. Reproduces on 0.31.0, 0.32.0, 0.33.0, and main. Pure-Python renderer bug, platform-independent. Fix PR open and marked ready/verified.
  3. DFlash acceptance collapse at TP>1 — Issue #66387. MiMo-V2.6-Flash-MOPD drafter; fine at TP1, degrades with tensor parallelism on 8-GPU NVLink. No fix linked yet.
  4. SM120 CUDA graph capture broken → severe decode slowdown — Issue #56892. DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash on 8× RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell with --enforce-eager; CUDA graphs unusable on SM120. Requested fix prioritization.
  5. Forced named tool choice ~11× slower on A100 vs prior version — Issue #65564. Qwen3.5-9B, regression from v0.27.1 → v0.31.0; tool_choice="auto" is fast.
  6. EagleMistralLarge3 AttributeError: 'use_mha' — Issue #43298. Speculative decoding crash on Mistral-Large-3-675B, 8×H200, still open.
  7. KV-offload re-queueing stall, 1.0–1.8 s — Issue #62532. Async KV pulls via OffloadingConnector + p2p/RDMA (NixlConnector). RFC proposes front-of-queue re-admission. Related promotion-lifecycle redesign in #66782.
  8. Host-buffer race in DSA indexer ShardQ path — PR #66052. Pinned buffers reused across steps could be overwritten by async scheduling before the copy runs; fix stages indices in fresh host memory each step.
  9. Batch-invariance / cuBLAS routing — withdrawn — Issue #65569 (closed). The proposal was withdrawn after finding cuBLAS is not batch-invariant for all shapes (narrow MoE router layers fail; boundary depends on K, workspace env vars, and GPU). Useful negative result for anyone depending on batch invariance.
  10. NVIDIA nightly CI failures — Issue #67307, now closed; tracked across several nightlies.

6. What This Means for Application Developers

  • If you serve DeepSeek-V4-Flash-Base with DeepEP low-latency on H200, apply the SwiGLU clamp fix (#68084) — the failure mode is silent numerical corruption that would corrupt evals and agent reasoning long before it throws.
  • Tool-calling code that passes user-influenced tool names should route around the gpt-oss 500 (#65770). If you build agents with gpt-oss and reconstruct prior tool calls into history, sanitize tool_call.name until the fix lands.
  • Don't rely on the assumption that "auto" and explicit tool routing are equivalent across frontends (#66858). If you are evaluating the Rust frontend, pin your gateway semantics and test tools + response_format + tool_choice="auto" explicitly.
  • Agent and multi-turn workloads on hybrid models (GDN + full attention) face a real TTFT tax when enabling --prefix-match-unit on the Triton/FLA GDN backend (~30 ms request-level). Measure against your trace mix before enabling (#67674).
  • RL and continual-learning loops should not build on pre-Rev-2 weight-reload behavior — it produced silent staleness in exactly the attention variants (MLA) that modern training pipelines use (#54477).
  • KV-offload-heavy deployments can expect 1.0–1.8 s stalls around completed async KV pulls today; if you run tiered offload with RoCE RDMA secondary tiers, track #62532 and #66782, which together redesign promotion timing and pinning semantics.
